## Read the SCA status of the payment cancellation's authorisation

<a id="opIdgetPaymentCancellationScaStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payments/domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-isr/1234-wertiq-983/cancellation-authorisations/123auth456 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721'
```

`GET /v1/{payment-service}/{payment-product}/{paymentId}/cancellation-authorisations/{authorisationId}`

This method returns the SCA status of a payment initiation's authorisation sub-resource.


<h3 id="read-the-sca-status-of-the-payment-cancellations-authorisation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment-service|path|string|true|Payment service:<br><br>Possible values are:<br>* payments<br>* bulk-payments<br>* periodic-payments<br>|
|payment-product|path|string|true|The addressed payment product endpoint, e.g. for SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT).<br>The ASPSP will publish which of the payment products/endpoints will be supported.<br><br>The following payment products are supported:<br>  - domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-isr<br>  - domestic-swiss-credit-transfers<br>  - domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-qr<br>  - domestic-swiss-foreign-credit-transfers<br>  - swiss-sepa-credit-transfers<br>  - swiss-cross-border-credit-transfers<br>  - pain.001-sepa-credit-transfers<br>  - pain.001-cross-border-credit-transfers<br>  - pain.001-swiss-six-credit-transfers<br><br>**Remark:** For all SEPA Credit Transfer based endpoints which accept XML encoding,<br>the XML pain.001 schemes provided by EPC are supported by the ASPSP as a minimum for the body content.<br>Further XML schemes might be supported by some communities.<br><br>**Remark:** For cross-border and TARGET-2 payments only community wide pain.001 schemes do exist.<br>There are plenty of country specificic scheme variants.<br>|
|paymentId|path|[paymentId](#schemapaymentid)|true|Resource identification of the generated payment initiation resource.|
|authorisationId|path|[authorisationId](#schemaauthorisationid)|true|Resource identification of the related SCA.|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding http request IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|payment-service|payments|
|payment-service|bulk-payments|
|payment-service|periodic-payments|
|payment-product|domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-isr|
|payment-product|domestic-swiss-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-qr|
|payment-product|domestic-swiss-foreign-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|swiss-sepa-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|swiss-cross-border-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|pain.001-sepa-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|pain.001-cross-border-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|pain.001-swiss-six-credit-transfers|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Update PSU data for payment initiation cancellation

<a id="opIdupdatePaymentCancellationPsuData"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payments/domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-isr/1234-wertiq-983/cancellation-authorisations/123auth456 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -d '{
    "confirmationCode": "2256ffgh"
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/{payment-service}/{payment-product}/{paymentId}/cancellation-authorisations/{authorisationId}`

This method updates PSU data on the cancellation authorisation resource if needed. 
It may authorise a cancellation of the payment within the Embedded SCA Approach where needed.

Independently from the SCA Approach it supports e.g. the selection of
the authentication method and a non-SCA PSU authentication.

There are several possible update PSU data requests in the context of a cancellation authorisation within the payment initiation services needed, 
which depends on the SCA approach:

* Redirect SCA Approach:
  A specific Update PSU data request is applicable for 
    * the selection of authentication methods, before choosing the actual SCA approach.
* Decoupled SCA Approach:
  A specific Update PSU data request is only applicable for
  * adding the PSU Identification, if not provided yet in the payment initiation request or the Account Information Consent Request, or if no OAuth2 access token is used, or
  * the selection of authentication methods.
* Embedded SCA Approach: 
  The Update PSU data request might be used 
  * to add credentials as a first factor authentication data of the PSU and
  * to select the authentication method and
  * transaction authorisation.

The SCA approach might depend on the chosen SCA method. 
For that reason, the following possible update PSU data request can apply to all SCA approaches:

* Select an SCA method in case of several SCA methods are available for the customer.

There are the following request types on this access path:
  * Update PSU identification
  * Update PSU authentication
  * Select PSU autorization method 
    WARNING: This method needs a reduced header, 
    therefore many optional elements are not present. 
    Maybe in a later version the access path will change.
  * Transaction Authorisation
    WARNING: This method needs a reduced header, 
    therefore many optional elements are not present. 
    Maybe in a later version the access path will change.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "confirmationCode": "2256ffgh"
}
```

<h3 id="update-psu-data-for-payment-initiation-cancellation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment-service|path|string|true|Payment service:<br><br>Possible values are:<br>* payments<br>* bulk-payments<br>* periodic-payments<br>|
|payment-product|path|string|true|The addressed payment product endpoint, e.g. for SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT).<br>The ASPSP will publish which of the payment products/endpoints will be supported.<br><br>The following payment products are supported:<br>  - domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-isr<br>  - domestic-swiss-credit-transfers<br>  - domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-qr<br>  - domestic-swiss-foreign-credit-transfers<br>  - swiss-sepa-credit-transfers<br>  - swiss-cross-border-credit-transfers<br>  - pain.001-sepa-credit-transfers<br>  - pain.001-cross-border-credit-transfers<br>  - pain.001-swiss-six-credit-transfers<br><br>**Remark:** For all SEPA Credit Transfer based endpoints which accept XML encoding,<br>the XML pain.001 schemes provided by EPC are supported by the ASPSP as a minimum for the body content.<br>Further XML schemes might be supported by some communities.<br><br>**Remark:** For cross-border and TARGET-2 payments only community wide pain.001 schemes do exist.<br>There are plenty of country specificic scheme variants.<br>|
|paymentId|path|[paymentId](#schemapaymentid)|true|Resource identification of the generated payment initiation resource.|
|authorisationId|path|[authorisationId](#schemaauthorisationid)|true|Resource identification of the related SCA.|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-ID|header|string|false|Client ID of the PSU in the ASPSP client interface.<br><br>Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation.<br><br>It might be contained even if an OAuth2 based authentication was performed in a pre-step or an OAuth2 based SCA was performed in an preceding<br>AIS service in the same session.<br>In this case the ASPSP might check whether PSU-ID and token match,<br>according to ASPSP documentation.<br>|
|PSU-ID-Type|header|string|false|Type of the PSU-ID, needed in scenarios where PSUs have several PSU-IDs as access possibility.<br><br>In this case, the mean and use are then defined in the ASPSP's documentation.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID-Type|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding http request IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|
|body|body|object \| [updatePsuAuthentication](#schemaupdatepsuauthentication) \| [selectPsuAuthenticationMethod](#schemaselectpsuauthenticationmethod) \| [transactionAuthorisation](#schematransactionauthorisation) \| [authorisationConfirmation](#schemaauthorisationconfirmation)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[updatePsuAuthentication](#schemaupdatepsuauthentication)|false|Content of the body of a Update PSU authentication request<br><br>Password subfield is used.<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[selectPsuAuthenticationMethod](#schemaselectpsuauthenticationmethod)|false|Content of the body of a Select PSU authentication method request<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[transactionAuthorisation](#schematransactionauthorisation)|false|Content of the body of a transaction authorisation request<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[authorisationConfirmation](#schemaauthorisationconfirmation)|false|Content of the body of an authorisation confirmation request<br>|

|---|---|
|payment-service|payments|
|payment-service|bulk-payments|
|payment-service|periodic-payments|
|payment-product|domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-isr|
|payment-product|domestic-swiss-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-qr|
|payment-product|domestic-swiss-foreign-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|swiss-sepa-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|swiss-cross-border-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|pain.001-sepa-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|pain.001-cross-border-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|pain.001-swiss-six-credit-transfers|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Payment initiation status request

<a id="opIdgetPaymentInitiationStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payments/domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-isr/1234-wertiq-983/status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721'
```

`GET /v1/{payment-service}/{payment-product}/{paymentId}/status`

Check the transaction status of a payment initiation.

<h3 id="payment-initiation-status-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment-service|path|string|true|Payment service:<br><br>Possible values are:<br>* payments<br>* bulk-payments<br>* periodic-payments<br>|
|payment-product|path|string|true|The addressed payment product endpoint, e.g. for SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT).<br>The ASPSP will publish which of the payment products/endpoints will be supported.<br><br>The following payment products are supported:<br>  - domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-isr<br>  - domestic-swiss-credit-transfers<br>  - domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-qr<br>  - domestic-swiss-foreign-credit-transfers<br>  - swiss-sepa-credit-transfers<br>  - swiss-cross-border-credit-transfers<br>  - pain.001-sepa-credit-transfers<br>  - pain.001-cross-border-credit-transfers<br>  - pain.001-swiss-six-credit-transfers<br><br>**Remark:** For all SEPA Credit Transfer based endpoints which accept XML encoding,<br>the XML pain.001 schemes provided by EPC are supported by the ASPSP as a minimum for the body content.<br>Further XML schemes might be supported by some communities.<br><br>**Remark:** For cross-border and TARGET-2 payments only community wide pain.001 schemes do exist.<br>There are plenty of country specificic scheme variants.<br>|
|paymentId|path|[paymentId](#schemapaymentid)|true|Resource identification of the generated payment initiation resource.|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding http request IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|payment-service|payments|
|payment-service|bulk-payments|
|payment-service|periodic-payments|
|payment-product|domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-isr|
|payment-product|domestic-swiss-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-qr|
|payment-product|domestic-swiss-foreign-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|swiss-sepa-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|swiss-cross-border-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|pain.001-sepa-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|pain.001-cross-border-credit-transfers|
|payment-product|pain.001-swiss-six-credit-transfers|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

<h1 id="swiss-nextgen-banking-api-framework-confirmation-of-funds-service-piis">Confirmation of Funds Service (PIIS)</h1>

Confirmation of Funds Service (PIIS) returns a confirmation of funds request at the ASPSP.


## Confirmation of funds request

<a id="opIdcheckAvailabilityOfFunds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/funds-confirmations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -d '{
    "account": {
      "iban": "DE23100120020123456789"
    },
    "cardNumber": "12345678901234",
    "instructedAmount": {
      "amount": "123",
      "currency": "EUR"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/funds-confirmations`

Creates a confirmation of funds request at the ASPSP. Checks whether a specific amount is available at point of time of the request on an account linked to a given tuple card issuer(TPP)/card number, or addressed by IBAN and TPP respectively.
If the related extended services are used a conditional Consent-ID is contained in the header. This field is contained but commented out in this specification.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account": {
    "iban": "DE23100120020123456789"
  },
  "cardNumber": "12345678901234",
  "instructedAmount": {
    "amount": "123",
    "currency": "EUR"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="confirmation-of-funds-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Authorization|header|[authorization](#schemaauthorization)|false|This field  might be used in case where a consent was agreed between ASPSP and PSU through an OAuth2 based protocol,<br>facilitated by the TPP.<br>|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|body|body|[confirmationOfFunds](#schemaconfirmationoffunds)|true|Request body for a confirmation of funds request.<br>|
|» account|body|[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)|true|Reference to an account by either<br>  * IBAN, of a payment accounts, or<br>  * otherAccountIdentification, for payment accounts if there is no IBAN<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 CashAccount16-CH_IdTpCcy<br>|
|» cardNumber|body|string|false|Card Number of the card issued by the PIISP.<br>Should be delivered if available.<br>|
|» instructedAmount|body|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|
|» payee|body|string|false|Name payee.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "fundsAvailable": "true"
}
```

<h3 id="confirmation-of-funds-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[Error400_NG_AIS](#schemaerror400_ng_ais)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[Error401_NG_PIIS](#schemaerror401_ng_piis)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[Error403_NG_PIIS](#schemaerror403_ng_piis)|
|404|Not Found|Not found|[Error404_NG_PIIS](#schemaerror404_ng_piis)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method Not Allowed|[Error405_NG_PIIS](#schemaerror405_ng_piis)|
|406|Not Acceptable|Not Acceptable|None|
|408|Request Timeout|Request Timeout|None|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|[Error409_NG_PIIS](#schemaerror409_ng_piis)|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported Media Type|None|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too Many Requests|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error|None|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service Unavailable|None|

<h3 id="confirmation-of-funds-request-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fundsAvailable|[fundsAvailable](#schemafundsavailable)|true|none|Equals true if sufficient funds are available at the time of the request, false otherwise.<br><br>This datalemenet is allways contained in a confirmation of funds response.<br><br>This data element is contained in a payment status response, <br>if supported by the ASPSP, if a funds check has been performed and <br>if the transactionStatus is "ACTC", "ACWC" or "ACCP".<br>|

<h1 id="swiss-nextgen-banking-api-framework-account-information-service-ais">Account Information Service (AIS)</h1>

The Account Information Service (AIS) offers the following services:
  * Transaction reports for a given account or card account including balances if applicable
  * Balances of a given account or card account
  * A list of available accounts or card account
  * Account details of a given account or card account or of the list of all accessible accounts or card account  relative to a granted consent


## Read account list

<a id="opIdgetAccountList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/accounts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -H 'Consent-ID: string'
```

`GET /v1/accounts`

Read the identifiers of the available payment account together with 
booking balance information, depending on the consent granted.

It is assumed that a consent of the PSU to this access is already given and stored on the ASPSP system.
The addressed list of accounts depends then on the PSU ID and the stored consent addressed by consentId,
respectively the OAuth2 access token.

Returns all identifiers of the accounts, to which an account access has been granted to through
the /consents endpoint by the PSU.
In addition, relevant information about the accounts and hyperlinks to corresponding account
information resources are provided if a related consent has been already granted.

Remark: Note that the /consents endpoint optionally offers to grant an access on all available
payment accounts of a PSU.
In this case, this endpoint will deliver the information about all available payment accounts
of the PSU at this ASPSP.


<h3 id="read-account-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|withBalance|query|boolean|false|If contained, this function reads the list of accessible payment accounts including the booking balance,<br>if granted by the PSU in the related consent and available by the ASPSP.<br>This parameter might be ignored by the ASPSP.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|Consent-ID|header|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|This then contains the consentId of the related AIS consent, which was performed prior to this payment initiation.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request<br>IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>It shall be contained if and only if this request was actively initiated by the PSU.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Read account details

<a id="opIdreadAccountDetails"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/accounts/qwer3456tzui7890 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -H 'Consent-ID: string'
```

`GET /v1/accounts/{account-id}`

Reads details about an account, with balances where required. 
It is assumed that a consent of the PSU to 
this access is already given and stored on the ASPSP system. 
The addressed details of this account depends then on the stored consent addressed by consentId, 
respectively the OAuth2 access token.

**NOTE:** The account-id can represent a multicurrency account.
In this case the currency code is set to "XXX".

Give detailed information about the addressed account.

Give detailed information about the addressed account together with balance information


<h3 id="read-account-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account-id|path|[accountId](#schemaaccountid)|true|This identification is denoting the addressed (card) account. <br>The account-id is retrieved by using a "Read Account List" or "Read Card Account list" call. <br>The account-id is the "resourceId" attribute of the account structure. <br>Its value is constant at least throughout the lifecycle of a given consent.<br>|
|withBalance|query|boolean|false|If contained, this function reads the list of accessible payment accounts including the booking balance,<br>if granted by the PSU in the related consent and available by the ASPSP.<br>This parameter might be ignored by the ASPSP.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|Consent-ID|header|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|This then contains the consentId of the related AIS consent, which was performed prior to this payment initiation.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request<br>IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>It shall be contained if and only if this request was actively initiated by the PSU.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Read balance

<a id="opIdgetBalances"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/accounts/qwer3456tzui7890/balances \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -H 'Consent-ID: string'
```

`GET /v1/accounts/{account-id}/balances`

Reads account data from a given account addressed by "account-id". 

**Remark:** This account-id can be a tokenised identification due to data protection reason since the path 
information might be logged on intermediary servers within the ASPSP sphere. 
This account-id then can be retrieved by the "Get account list" call.

The account-id is constant at least throughout the lifecycle of a given consent.


<h3 id="read-balance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account-id|path|[accountId](#schemaaccountid)|true|This identification is denoting the addressed (card) account. <br>The account-id is retrieved by using a "Read Account List" or "Read Card Account list" call. <br>The account-id is the "resourceId" attribute of the account structure. <br>Its value is constant at least throughout the lifecycle of a given consent.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|Consent-ID|header|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|This then contains the consentId of the related AIS consent, which was performed prior to this payment initiation.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request<br>IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>It shall be contained if and only if this request was actively initiated by the PSU.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Read transaction list of an account

<a id="opIdgetTransactionList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/v1/accounts/qwer3456tzui7890/transactions?bookingStatus=information' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -H 'Consent-ID: string'
```

`GET /v1/accounts/{account-id}/transactions`

Read transaction reports or transaction lists of a given account ddressed by "account-id", depending on the steering parameter
"bookingStatus" together with balances.

For a given account, additional parameters are e.g. the attributes "dateFrom" and "dateTo".
The ASPSP might add balance information, if transaction lists without balances are not supported.


<h3 id="read-transaction-list-of-an-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account-id|path|[accountId](#schemaaccountid)|true|This identification is denoting the addressed (card) account. <br>The account-id is retrieved by using a "Read Account List" or "Read Card Account list" call. <br>The account-id is the "resourceId" attribute of the account structure. <br>Its value is constant at least throughout the lifecycle of a given consent.<br>|
|dateFrom|query|string(date)|false|Conditional: Starting date (inclusive the date dateFrom) of the transaction list, mandated if no delta access is required<br>and if bookingStatus does not equal "information".<br><br>For booked transactions, the relevant date is the booking date. <br><br>For pending transactions, the relevant date is the entry date, which may not be transparent <br>neither in this API nor other channels of the ASPSP.<br>|
|dateTo|query|string(date)|false|End date (inclusive the data dateTo) of the transaction list, default is "now" if not given.<br><br>Might be ignored if a delta function is used.<br><br>For booked transactions, the relevant date is the booking date.<br><br>For pending transactions, the relevant date is the entry date, which may not be transparent<br>neither in this API nor other channels of the ASPSP.<br>|
|entryReferenceFrom|query|string|false|This data attribute is indicating that the AISP is in favour to get all transactions after<br>the transaction with identification entryReferenceFrom alternatively to the above defined period.<br>This is a implementation of a delta access.<br>If this data element is contained, the entries "dateFrom" and "dateTo" might be ignored by the ASPSP<br>if a delta report is supported.<br><br>Optional if supported by API provider.<br>|
|bookingStatus|query|string|true|Permitted codes are <br>  * "information",<br>  * "booked",<br>  * "pending", and <br>  * "both"<br>"booked" shall be supported by the ASPSP.<br>To support the "pending" and "both" feature is optional for the ASPSP,<br>Error code if not supported in the online banking frontend<br>|
|deltaList|query|boolean|false|This data attribute is indicating that the AISP is in favour to get all transactions after the last report access for this PSU on the addressed account. This is another implementation of a delta access-report.<br>This delta indicator might be rejected by the ASPSP if this function is not supported.<br>Optional if supported by API provider|
|withBalance|query|boolean|false|If contained, this function reads the list of accessible payment accounts including the booking balance,<br>if granted by the PSU in the related consent and available by the ASPSP.<br>This parameter might be ignored by the ASPSP.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|Consent-ID|header|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|This then contains the consentId of the related AIS consent, which was performed prior to this payment initiation.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request<br>IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>It shall be contained if and only if this request was actively initiated by the PSU.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|bookingStatus|information|
|bookingStatus|booked|
|bookingStatus|pending|
|bookingStatus|both|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Read transaction details

<a id="opIdgetTransactionDetails"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/accounts/qwer3456tzui7890/transactions/3dc3d5b3-7023-4848-9853-f5400a64e80f \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -H 'Consent-ID: string'
```

`GET /v1/accounts/{account-id}/transactions/{transactionId}`

Reads transaction details from a given transaction addressed by "transactionId" on a given account addressed by "account-id".
This call is only available on transactions as reported in a JSON format.

**Remark:** Please note that the PATH might be already given in detail by the corresponding entry of the response of the
"Read Transaction List" call within the _links subfield.


<h3 id="read-transaction-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account-id|path|[accountId](#schemaaccountid)|true|This identification is denoting the addressed (card) account. <br>The account-id is retrieved by using a "Read Account List" or "Read Card Account list" call. <br>The account-id is the "resourceId" attribute of the account structure. <br>Its value is constant at least throughout the lifecycle of a given consent.<br>|
|transactionId|path|[transactionId](#schematransactionid)|true|This identification is given by the attribute transactionId of the corresponding entry of a transaction list.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|Consent-ID|header|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|This then contains the consentId of the related AIS consent, which was performed prior to this payment initiation.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request<br>IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>It shall be contained if and only if this request was actively initiated by the PSU.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[Error401_NG_AIS](#schemaerror401_ng_ais)|

|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error|None|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service Unavailable|None|

## Create consent

<a id="opIdcreateConsent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/consents \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -H 'PSU-IP-Address: 192.168.8.78' \
  -d '{
    "access": {
      "balances": [],
      "transactions": []
    },
    "frequencyPerDay": 4,
    "recurringIndicator": "true",
    "validUntil": "2017-11-01"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/consents`

This method create a consent resource, defining access rights to dedicated accounts of 
a given PSU-ID. These accounts are addressed explicitly in the method as 
parameters as a core function.

**Side Effects**
When this consent request is a request where the "recurringIndicator" equals "true",
and if it exists already a former consent for recurring access on account information 
for the addressed PSU, then the former consent automatically expires as soon as the new 
consent request is authorised by the PSU.

Optional Extension:
As an option, an ASPSP might optionally accept a specific access right on the access on all PSD2 related services for all available accounts.

As another option an ASPSP might optionally also accept a command, where only access rights are inserted without mentioning the addressed account. 
The relation to accounts is then handled afterwards between PSU and ASPSP. 
This option is not supported for the Embedded SCA Approach. 
As a last option, an ASPSP might in addition accept a command with access rights
  * to see the list of available payment accounts or
  * to see the list of available payment accounts with balances.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access": {
    "balances": [],
    "transactions": []
  },
  "frequencyPerDay": 4,
  "recurringIndicator": "true",
  "validUntil": "2017-11-01"
}
```

<h3 id="create-consent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-ID|header|string|false|Client ID of the PSU in the ASPSP client interface.<br><br>Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation.<br><br>It might be contained even if an OAuth2 based authentication was performed in a pre-step or an OAuth2 based SCA was performed in an preceding<br>AIS service in the same session.<br>In this case the ASPSP might check whether PSU-ID and token match,<br>according to ASPSP documentation.<br>|
|PSU-ID-Type|header|string|false|Type of the PSU-ID, needed in scenarios where PSUs have several PSU-IDs as access possibility.<br><br>In this case, the mean and use are then defined in the ASPSP's documentation.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID-Type|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|TPP-Redirect-Preferred|header|boolean|false|If it equals "true", the TPP prefers a redirect over an embedded SCA approach.<br>If it equals "false", the TPP prefers not to be redirected for SCA. The ASPSP will then choose between the Embedded or the Decoupled<br>SCA approach, depending on the choice of the SCA procedure by the TPP/PSU.<br>If the parameter is not used, the ASPSP will choose the SCA approach to be applied depending on the SCA method chosen by the<br>TPP/PSU.<br>|
|TPP-Redirect-URI|header|string(uri)|false|URI of the TPP, where the transaction flow shall be redirected to after a Redirect.<br><br>Mandated for the Redirect SCA Approach, specifically<br>when TPP-Redirect-Preferred equals "true".<br>It is recommended to always use this header field.<br><br>**Remark for Future:**<br>This field might be changed to mandatory in the next version of the specification.<br>|
|TPP-Nok-Redirect-URI|header|string(uri)|false|If this URI is contained, the TPP is asking to redirect the transaction flow to this address instead of the TPP-Redirect-URI in case<br>of a negative result of the redirect SCA method. This might be ignored by the ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Explicit-Authorisation-Preferred|header|boolean|false|If it equals "true", the TPP prefers to start the authorisation process separately,<br>e.g. because of the usage of a signing basket.<br>This preference might be ignored by the ASPSP, if a signing basket is not supported as functionality.<br><br>If it equals "false" or if the parameter is not used, there is no preference of the TPP.<br>This especially indicates that the TPP assumes a direct authorisation of the transaction in the next step,<br>without using a signing basket.<br>|
|TPP-Brand-Logging-Information|header|string|false|This header might be used by TPPs to inform the ASPSP about the brand used by the TPP towards the PSU. <br>This information is meant for logging entries to enhance communication between ASPSP and PSU or ASPSP and TPP. <br>This header might be ignored by the ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Notification-URI|header|string|false|URI for the Endpoint of the TPP-API to which the status of the payment initiation should be sent.<br>This header field may by ignored by the ASPSP.<br><br>For security reasons, it shall be ensured that the TPP-Notification-URI as introduced above is secured by the TPP eIDAS QWAC used for identification of the TPP. The following applies:<br><br>URIs which are provided by TPPs in TPP-Notification-URI shall comply with the domain secured by the eIDAS QWAC certificate of the TPP in the field CN or SubjectAltName of the certificate. Please note that in case of example-TPP.com as certificate entry TPP- Notification-URI like www.example-TPP.com/xs2a-client/v1/ASPSPidentifcation/mytransaction- id/notifications or notifications.example-TPP.com/xs2a-client/v1/ASPSPidentifcation/mytransaction- id/notifications would be compliant.<br><br>Wildcard definitions shall be taken into account for compliance checks by the ASPSP.<br> ASPSPs may respond with ASPSP-Notification-Support set to false, if the provided URIs do not comply.<br>|
|TPP-Notification-Content-Preferred|header|string|false|The string has the form<br><br>status=X1, ..., Xn<br><br>where Xi is one of the constants SCA, PROCESS, LAST and where constants are not<br>repeated.<br>The usage of the constants supports the of following semantics:<br><br>  SCA: A notification on every change of the scaStatus attribute for all related authorisation processes is preferred by the TPP.<br><br>  PROCESS: A notification on all changes of consentStatus or transactionStatus attributes is preferred by the TPP.<br>  LAST: Only a notification on the last consentStatus or transactionStatus as available in the XS2A interface is preferred by the TPP.<br><br>This header field may be ignored, if the ASPSP does not support resource notification services for the related TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|true|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding http request IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>If not available, the TPP shall use the IP Address used by the TPP when submitting this request.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|
|body|body|[consents](#schemaconsents)|false|Request body for a consents request.<br>|
|» access|body|[accountAccess](#schemaaccountaccess)|true|Requested access services for a consent.<br>|
|» combinedServiceIndicator|body|boolean|true|If "true" indicates that a payment initiation service will be addressed in the same "session".<br>|
|» frequencyPerDay|body|[frequencyPerDay](#schemafrequencyperday)|true|This field indicates the requested maximum frequency for an access without PSU involvement per day.<br>For a one-off access, this attribute is set to "1".<br><br>The frequency needs to be greater equal to one.<br><br>If not otherwise agreed bilaterally between TPP and ASPSP, the frequency is less equal to 4.<br>|
|» recurringIndicator|body|[recurringIndicator](#schemarecurringindicator)|true|"true", if the consent is for recurring access to the account data.<br><br>"false", if the consent is for one access to the account data.<br>|
|» validUntil|body|[validUntil](#schemavaliduntil)|true|This parameter is defining a valid until date (including the mentioned date) for the requested consent. <br>The content is the local ASPSP date in ISO-Date format, e.g. 2017-10-30.<br><br>Future dates might get adjusted by ASPSP. <br><br>If a maximal available date is requested, a date in far future is to be used: "9999-12-31". <br><br>In both cases the consent object to be retrieved by the get consent request will contain the adjusted date.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|[consentsResponse-201](#schemaconsentsresponse-201)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[Error400_NG_AIS](#schemaerror400_ng_ais)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[Error401_NG_AIS](#schemaerror401_ng_ais)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[Error403_NG_AIS](#schemaerror403_ng_ais)|
|404|Not Found|Not found|[Error404_NG_AIS](#schemaerror404_ng_ais)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method Not Allowed|[Error405_NG_AIS](#schemaerror405_ng_ais)|
|406|Not Acceptable|Not Acceptable|[Error406_NG_AIS](#schemaerror406_ng_ais)|
|408|Request Timeout|Request Timeout|None|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|[Error409_NG_AIS](#schemaerror409_ng_ais)|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported Media Type|None|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too Many Requests|[Error429_NG_AIS](#schemaerror429_ng_ais)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error|None|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service Unavailable|None|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|ASPSP-Notification-Content|string||The string has the form<br>status=X1, ..., Xn<br>where Xi is one of the constants SCA, PROCESS, LAST and where constants are not repeated.<br>The usage of the constants supports the following semantics<br>SCA - Notification on every change of the scaStatus attribute for all related authorisation processes is provided by the ASPSP for the related resource.<br>PROCESS - Notification on all changes of consentStatus or transactionStatus attributes is provided by the ASPSP for the related resource<br>LAST - Notification on the last consentStatus or transactionStatus as available in the XS2A interface is provided by the ASPSP for the related resource.<br>This field must be provided if the ASPSP-Notification-Support=true. The ASPSP might consider the notification content as preferred by the TPP, but can also respond independently of the preferred request<br>|
|201|ASPSP-Notification-Support|boolean||true if the ASPSP supports resource status notification services.<br><br>false if the ASPSP supports resource status notification in general, but not for the current request.<br><br>Not used, if resource status notification services are generally not supported by the ASPSP.<br><br>Shall be supported if the ASPSP supports resource status notification services.<br>|
|201|ASPSP-SCA-Approach|string||This data element must be contained, if the SCA Approach is already fixed.<br>Possible values are<br>  * EMBEDDED<br>  * DECOUPLED<br>  * REDIRECT<br>The OAuth SCA approach will be subsumed by REDIRECT.<br>|
|201|Location|string||Location of the created resource.<br>|
|201|X-Request-ID|string||ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|400|Location|string||Location of the created resource.<br>|

## Get consent request

<a id="opIdgetConsentInformation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/consents/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721'
```

`GET /v1/consents/{consentId}`

Returns the content of an account information consent object. 
This is returning the data for the TPP especially in cases, 
where the consent was directly managed between ASPSP and PSU e.g. in a redirect SCA Approach.


<h3 id="get-consent-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|consentId|path|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|ID of the corresponding consent object as returned by an account information consent request.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request<br>IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>It shall be contained if and only if this request was actively initiated by the PSU.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Delete Consent

<a id="opIddeleteConsent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/consents/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721'
```

`DELETE /v1/consents/{consentId}`

The TPP can delete an account information consent object if needed.

<h3 id="delete-consent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|consentId|path|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|ID of the corresponding consent object as returned by an account information consent request.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request<br>IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>It shall be contained if and only if this request was actively initiated by the PSU.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Get consent authorisation sub-resources request

<a id="opIdgetConsentAuthorisation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/consents/string/authorisations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721'
```

`GET /v1/consents/{consentId}/authorisations`

Return a list of all authorisation subresources IDs which have been created.

This function returns an array of hyperlinks to all generated authorisation sub-resources.


<h3 id="get-consent-authorisation-sub-resources-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|consentId|path|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|ID of the corresponding consent object as returned by an account information consent request.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request<br>IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>It shall be contained if and only if this request was actively initiated by the PSU.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values
