## Start the authorisation process for a consent

<a id="opIdstartConsentAuthorisation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/consents/string/authorisations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -d 'null'
```

`POST /v1/consents/{consentId}/authorisations`

Create an authorisation sub-resource and start the authorisation process of a consent.
The message might in addition transmit authentication and authorisation related data.

his method is iterated n times for a n times SCA authorisation in a
corporate context, each creating an own authorisation sub-endpoint for
the corresponding PSU authorising the consent.

The ASPSP might make the usage of this access method unnecessary,
since the related authorisation resource will be automatically created by
the ASPSP after the submission of the consent data with the first POST consents call.

The start authorisation process is a process which is needed for creating a new authorisation
or cancellation sub-resource.

This applies in the following scenarios:

  * The ASPSP has indicated with an 'startAuthorisation' hyperlink in the preceding Payment 
    initiation response that an explicit start of the authorisation process is needed by the TPP. 
    The 'startAuthorisation' hyperlink can transport more information about data which needs to be 
    uploaded by using the extended forms:
    * 'startAuthorisationWithPsuIdentfication', 
    * 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication' 
    * 'startAuthorisationWithEncryptedPsuAuthentication'
    * 'startAuthorisationWithAuthentciationMethodSelection'
  * The related payment initiation cannot yet be executed since a multilevel SCA is mandated.
  * The ASPSP has indicated with an 'startAuthorisation' hyperlink in the preceding 
    payment cancellation response that an explicit start of the authorisation process is needed by the TPP. 
    The 'startAuthorisation' hyperlink can transport more information about data which needs to be uploaded 
    by using the extended forms as indicated above.
  * The related payment cancellation request cannot be applied yet since a multilevel SCA is mandate for
    executing the cancellation.
  * The signing basket needs to be authorised yet.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="start-the-authorisation-process-for-a-consent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|consentId|path|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|ID of the corresponding consent object as returned by an account information consent request.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-ID|header|string|false|Client ID of the PSU in the ASPSP client interface.<br><br>Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation.<br><br>It might be contained even if an OAuth2 based authentication was performed in a pre-step or an OAuth2 based SCA was performed in an preceding<br>AIS service in the same session.<br>In this case the ASPSP might check whether PSU-ID and token match,<br>according to ASPSP documentation.<br>|
|PSU-ID-Type|header|string|false|Type of the PSU-ID, needed in scenarios where PSUs have several PSU-IDs as access possibility.<br><br>In this case, the mean and use are then defined in the ASPSP's documentation.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID-Type|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|TPP-Redirect-Preferred|header|boolean|false|If it equals "true", the TPP prefers a redirect over an embedded SCA approach.<br>If it equals "false", the TPP prefers not to be redirected for SCA. The ASPSP will then choose between the Embedded or the Decoupled<br>SCA approach, depending on the choice of the SCA procedure by the TPP/PSU.<br>If the parameter is not used, the ASPSP will choose the SCA approach to be applied depending on the SCA method chosen by the<br>TPP/PSU.<br>|
|TPP-Redirect-URI|header|string(uri)|false|URI of the TPP, where the transaction flow shall be redirected to after a Redirect.<br><br>Mandated for the Redirect SCA Approach, specifically<br>when TPP-Redirect-Preferred equals "true".<br>It is recommended to always use this header field.<br><br>**Remark for Future:**<br>This field might be changed to mandatory in the next version of the specification.<br>|
|TPP-Nok-Redirect-URI|header|string(uri)|false|If this URI is contained, the TPP is asking to redirect the transaction flow to this address instead of the TPP-Redirect-URI in case<br>of a negative result of the redirect SCA method. This might be ignored by the ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Notification-URI|header|string|false|URI for the Endpoint of the TPP-API to which the status of the payment initiation should be sent.<br>This header field may by ignored by the ASPSP.<br><br>For security reasons, it shall be ensured that the TPP-Notification-URI as introduced above is secured by the TPP eIDAS QWAC used for identification of the TPP. The following applies:<br><br>URIs which are provided by TPPs in TPP-Notification-URI shall comply with the domain secured by the eIDAS QWAC certificate of the TPP in the field CN or SubjectAltName of the certificate. Please note that in case of example-TPP.com as certificate entry TPP- Notification-URI like www.example-TPP.com/xs2a-client/v1/ASPSPidentifcation/mytransaction- id/notifications or notifications.example-TPP.com/xs2a-client/v1/ASPSPidentifcation/mytransaction- id/notifications would be compliant.<br><br>Wildcard definitions shall be taken into account for compliance checks by the ASPSP.<br> ASPSPs may respond with ASPSP-Notification-Support set to false, if the provided URIs do not comply.<br>|
|TPP-Notification-Content-Preferred|header|string|false|The string has the form<br><br>status=X1, ..., Xn<br><br>where Xi is one of the constants SCA, PROCESS, LAST and where constants are not<br>repeated.<br>The usage of the constants supports the of following semantics:<br><br>  SCA: A notification on every change of the scaStatus attribute for all related authorisation processes is preferred by the TPP.<br><br>  PROCESS: A notification on all changes of consentStatus or transactionStatus attributes is preferred by the TPP.<br>  LAST: Only a notification on the last consentStatus or transactionStatus as available in the XS2A interface is preferred by the TPP.<br><br>This header field may be ignored, if the ASPSP does not support resource notification services for the related TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request<br>IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>It shall be contained if and only if this request was actively initiated by the PSU.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|
|body|body|object \| [updatePsuAuthentication](#schemaupdatepsuauthentication) \| [selectPsuAuthenticationMethod](#schemaselectpsuauthenticationmethod) \| [transactionAuthorisation](#schematransactionauthorisation)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[updatePsuAuthentication](#schemaupdatepsuauthentication)|false|Content of the body of a Update PSU authentication request<br><br>Password subfield is used.<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[selectPsuAuthenticationMethod](#schemaselectpsuauthenticationmethod)|false|Content of the body of a Select PSU authentication method request<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[transactionAuthorisation](#schematransactionauthorisation)|false|Content of the body of a transaction authorisation request<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Read the SCA status of the consent authorisation

<a id="opIdgetConsentScaStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/consents/string/authorisations/123auth456 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721'
```

`GET /v1/consents/{consentId}/authorisations/{authorisationId}`

This method returns the SCA status of a consent initiation's authorisation sub-resource.


<h3 id="read-the-sca-status-of-the-consent-authorisation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|consentId|path|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|ID of the corresponding consent object as returned by an account information consent request.<br>|
|authorisationId|path|[authorisationId](#schemaauthorisationid)|true|Resource identification of the related SCA.|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request<br>IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>It shall be contained if and only if this request was actively initiated by the PSU.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Update PSU Data for consents

<a id="opIdupdateConsentsPsuData"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/consents/string/authorisations/123auth456 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -d '{
    "confirmationCode": "2256ffgh"
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/consents/{consentId}/authorisations/{authorisationId}`

This method update PSU data on the consents  resource if needed.
It may authorise a consent within the Embedded SCA Approach where needed.

Independently from the SCA Approach it supports e.g. the selection of
the authentication method and a non-SCA PSU authentication.

There are several possible update PSU data requests in the context of a consent request if needed, 
which depends on the SCA approach:

* Redirect SCA Approach:
  A specific Update PSU data request is applicable for 
    * the selection of authentication methods, before choosing the actual SCA approach.
* Decoupled SCA Approach:
  A specific update PSU data request is only applicable for
  * adding the PSU Identification, if not provided yet in the payment initiation request or the Account Information Consent Request, or if no OAuth2 access token is used, or
  * the selection of authentication methods.
* Embedded SCA Approach: 
  The Update PSU data request might be used 
  * to add credentials as a first factor authentication data of the PSU and
  * to select the authentication method and
  * transaction authorisation.

The SCA Approach might depend on the chosen SCA method. 
For that reason, the following possible update PSU data request can apply to all SCA approaches:

* Select an SCA method in case of several SCA methods are available for the customer.

There are the following request types on this access path:
  * Update PSU identification
  * Update PSU authentication
  * Select PSU autorization method 
    WARNING: This method needs a reduced header, 
    therefore many optional elements are not present. 
    Maybe in a later version the access path will change.
  * Transaction Authorisation
    WARNING: This method needs a reduced header, 
    therefore many optional elements are not present. 
    Maybe in a later version the access path will change.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "confirmationCode": "2256ffgh"
}
```

<h3 id="update-psu-data-for-consents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|consentId|path|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|ID of the corresponding consent object as returned by an account information consent request.<br>|
|authorisationId|path|[authorisationId](#schemaauthorisationid)|true|Resource identification of the related SCA.|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-ID|header|string|false|Client ID of the PSU in the ASPSP client interface.<br><br>Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation.<br><br>It might be contained even if an OAuth2 based authentication was performed in a pre-step or an OAuth2 based SCA was performed in an preceding<br>AIS service in the same session.<br>In this case the ASPSP might check whether PSU-ID and token match,<br>according to ASPSP documentation.<br>|
|PSU-ID-Type|header|string|false|Type of the PSU-ID, needed in scenarios where PSUs have several PSU-IDs as access possibility.<br><br>In this case, the mean and use are then defined in the ASPSP's documentation.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID-Type|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request<br>IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>It shall be contained if and only if this request was actively initiated by the PSU.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|
|body|body|object \| [updatePsuAuthentication](#schemaupdatepsuauthentication) \| [selectPsuAuthenticationMethod](#schemaselectpsuauthenticationmethod) \| [transactionAuthorisation](#schematransactionauthorisation) \| [authorisationConfirmation](#schemaauthorisationconfirmation)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[updatePsuAuthentication](#schemaupdatepsuauthentication)|false|Content of the body of a Update PSU authentication request<br><br>Password subfield is used.<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[selectPsuAuthenticationMethod](#schemaselectpsuauthenticationmethod)|false|Content of the body of a Select PSU authentication method request<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[transactionAuthorisation](#schematransactionauthorisation)|false|Content of the body of a transaction authorisation request<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[authorisationConfirmation](#schemaauthorisationconfirmation)|false|Content of the body of an authorisation confirmation request<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[Error401_NG_AIS](#schemaerror401_ng_ais)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[Error403_NG_AIS](#schemaerror403_ng_ais)|
|404|Not Found|Not found|[Error404_NG_AIS](#schemaerror404_ng_ais)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method Not Allowed|[Error405_NG_AIS](#schemaerror405_ng_ais)|
|406|Not Acceptable|Not Acceptable|[Error406_NG_AIS](#schemaerror406_ng_ais)|
|408|Request Timeout|Request Timeout|None|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|[Error409_NG_AIS](#schemaerror409_ng_ais)|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported Media Type|None|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too Many Requests|[Error429_NG_AIS](#schemaerror429_ng_ais)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error|None|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service Unavailable|None|

<h3 id="update-psu-data-for-consents-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[updatePsuIdenticationResponse](#schemaupdatepsuidenticationresponse)|false|none|Body of the JSON response for a successful update PSU identification request.|
|*oneOf*|[updatePsuAuthenticationResponse](#schemaupdatepsuauthenticationresponse)|false|none|Body of the JSON response for a successful update PSU authentication request.|
|*oneOf*|[selectPsuAuthenticationMethodResponse](#schemaselectpsuauthenticationmethodresponse)|false|none|Body of the JSON response for a successful select PSU authentication method request.|
|*oneOf*|[scaStatusResponse](#schemascastatusresponse)|false|none|Body of the JSON response with SCA Status.|
|*oneOf*|[authorisationConfirmationResponse](#schemaauthorisationconfirmationresponse)|false|none|Body of the JSON response for an authorisation confirmation request.|

## Consent status request

<a id="opIdgetConsentStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/consents/string/status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721'
```

`GET /v1/consents/{consentId}/status`

Read the status of an account information consent resource.

<h3 id="consent-status-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|consentId|path|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|ID of the corresponding consent object as returned by an account information consent request.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request<br>IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>It shall be contained if and only if this request was actively initiated by the PSU.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

<h1 id="swiss-nextgen-banking-api-framework-signing-baskets-service-sbs">Signing Baskets Service (SBS)</h1>

Signing basket methods are used for authorising several transactions and resp. or consents with one SCA operation.


## Create a signing basket resource

<a id="opIdcreateSigningBasket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/signing-baskets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -H 'PSU-IP-Address: 192.168.8.78' \
  -d '{
    "paymentIds": [
      "123qwert456789",
      "12345qwert7899"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/signing-baskets`

Create a signing basket resource for authorising several transactions with one SCA method. 
The resource identifications of these transactions are contained in the payload of this access method


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "paymentIds": [
    "123qwert456789",
    "12345qwert7899"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-signing-basket-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-ID|header|string|false|Client ID of the PSU in the ASPSP client interface.<br><br>Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation.<br><br>It might be contained even if an OAuth2 based authentication was performed in a pre-step or an OAuth2 based SCA was performed in an preceding<br>AIS service in the same session.<br>In this case the ASPSP might check whether PSU-ID and token match,<br>according to ASPSP documentation.<br>|
|PSU-ID-Type|header|string|false|Type of the PSU-ID, needed in scenarios where PSUs have several PSU-IDs as access possibility.<br><br>In this case, the mean and use are then defined in the ASPSP's documentation.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID-Type|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|Consent-ID|header|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|false|This data element may be contained, if the payment initiation transaction is part of a session, i.e. combined AIS/PIS service.<br>This then contains the consentId of the related AIS consent, which was performed prior to this payment initiation.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|true|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding http request IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>If not available, the TPP shall use the IP Address used by the TPP when submitting this request.<br>|
|TPP-Redirect-Preferred|header|boolean|false|If it equals "true", the TPP prefers a redirect over an embedded SCA approach.<br>If it equals "false", the TPP prefers not to be redirected for SCA. The ASPSP will then choose between the Embedded or the Decoupled<br>SCA approach, depending on the choice of the SCA procedure by the TPP/PSU.<br>If the parameter is not used, the ASPSP will choose the SCA approach to be applied depending on the SCA method chosen by the<br>TPP/PSU.<br>|
|TPP-Redirect-URI|header|string(uri)|false|URI of the TPP, where the transaction flow shall be redirected to after a Redirect.<br><br>Mandated for the Redirect SCA Approach, specifically<br>when TPP-Redirect-Preferred equals "true".<br>It is recommended to always use this header field.<br><br>**Remark for Future:**<br>This field might be changed to mandatory in the next version of the specification.<br>|
|TPP-Nok-Redirect-URI|header|string(uri)|false|If this URI is contained, the TPP is asking to redirect the transaction flow to this address instead of the TPP-Redirect-URI in case<br>of a negative result of the redirect SCA method. This might be ignored by the ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Explicit-Authorisation-Preferred|header|boolean|false|If it equals "true", the TPP prefers to start the authorisation process separately,<br>e.g. because of the usage of a signing basket.<br>This preference might be ignored by the ASPSP, if a signing basket is not supported as functionality.<br><br>If it equals "false" or if the parameter is not used, there is no preference of the TPP.<br>This especially indicates that the TPP assumes a direct authorisation of the transaction in the next step,<br>without using a signing basket.<br>|
|TPP-Notification-URI|header|string|false|URI for the Endpoint of the TPP-API to which the status of the payment initiation should be sent.<br>This header field may by ignored by the ASPSP.<br><br>For security reasons, it shall be ensured that the TPP-Notification-URI as introduced above is secured by the TPP eIDAS QWAC used for identification of the TPP. The following applies:<br><br>URIs which are provided by TPPs in TPP-Notification-URI shall comply with the domain secured by the eIDAS QWAC certificate of the TPP in the field CN or SubjectAltName of the certificate. Please note that in case of example-TPP.com as certificate entry TPP- Notification-URI like www.example-TPP.com/xs2a-client/v1/ASPSPidentifcation/mytransaction- id/notifications or notifications.example-TPP.com/xs2a-client/v1/ASPSPidentifcation/mytransaction- id/notifications would be compliant.<br><br>Wildcard definitions shall be taken into account for compliance checks by the ASPSP.<br> ASPSPs may respond with ASPSP-Notification-Support set to false, if the provided URIs do not comply.<br>|
|TPP-Notification-Content-Preferred|header|string|false|The string has the form<br><br>status=X1, ..., Xn<br><br>where Xi is one of the constants SCA, PROCESS, LAST and where constants are not<br>repeated.<br>The usage of the constants supports the of following semantics:<br><br>  SCA: A notification on every change of the scaStatus attribute for all related authorisation processes is preferred by the TPP.<br><br>  PROCESS: A notification on all changes of consentStatus or transactionStatus attributes is preferred by the TPP.<br>  LAST: Only a notification on the last consentStatus or transactionStatus as available in the XS2A interface is preferred by the TPP.<br><br>This header field may be ignored, if the ASPSP does not support resource notification services for the related TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|
|body|body|[signingBasket](#schemasigningbasket)|false|Request body for a confirmation of an establishing signing basket request.<br>|
|» consentIds|body|[consentIdList](#schemaconsentidlist)|false|A list of consentIds.|
|» paymentIds|body|[paymentIdList](#schemapaymentidlist)|false|A list of paymentIds.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|ASPSP-Notification-Content|string||The string has the form<br>status=X1, ..., Xn<br>where Xi is one of the constants SCA, PROCESS, LAST and where constants are not repeated.<br>The usage of the constants supports the following semantics<br>SCA - Notification on every change of the scaStatus attribute for all related authorisation processes is provided by the ASPSP for the related resource.<br>PROCESS - Notification on all changes of consentStatus or transactionStatus attributes is provided by the ASPSP for the related resource<br>LAST - Notification on the last consentStatus or transactionStatus as available in the XS2A interface is provided by the ASPSP for the related resource.<br>This field must be provided if the ASPSP-Notification-Support=true. The ASPSP might consider the notification content as preferred by the TPP, but can also respond independently of the preferred request<br>|
|201|ASPSP-Notification-Support|boolean||true if the ASPSP supports resource status notification services.<br><br>false if the ASPSP supports resource status notification in general, but not for the current request.<br><br>Not used, if resource status notification services are generally not supported by the ASPSP.<br><br>Shall be supported if the ASPSP supports resource status notification services.<br>|
|201|ASPSP-SCA-Approach|string||This data element must be contained, if the SCA Approach is already fixed.<br>Possible values are<br>  * EMBEDDED<br>  * DECOUPLED<br>  * REDIRECT<br>The OAuth SCA approach will be subsumed by REDIRECT.<br>|
|201|Location|string||Location of the created resource.<br>|

## Returns the content of an signing basket object

<a id="opIdgetSigningBasket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/signing-baskets/1234-basket-567 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721'
```

`GET /v1/signing-baskets/{basketId}`

Returns the content of a signing basket object.

<h3 id="returns-the-content-of-an-signing-basket-object-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|basketId|path|[basketId](#schemabasketid)|true|This identification of the corresponding signing basket object.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding http request IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Delete the signing basket

<a id="opIddeleteSigningBasket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/signing-baskets/1234-basket-567 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721'
```

`DELETE /v1/signing-baskets/{basketId}`

Delete the signing basket structure as long as no (partial) authorisation has yet been applied.
The undlerying transactions are not affected by this deletion.

Remark: The signing basket as such is not deletable after a first (partial) authorisation has been applied.
Nevertheless, single transactions might be cancelled on an individual basis on the XS2A interface.


<h3 id="delete-the-signing-basket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|basketId|path|[basketId](#schemabasketid)|true|This identification of the corresponding signing basket object.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding http request IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Get signing basket authorisation sub-resources request

<a id="opIdgetSigningBasketAuthorisation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/signing-baskets/1234-basket-567/authorisations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721'
```

`GET /v1/signing-baskets/{basketId}/authorisations`

Read a list of all authorisation subresources IDs which have been created.

This function returns an array of hyperlinks to all generated authorisation sub-resources.


<h3 id="get-signing-basket-authorisation-sub-resources-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|basketId|path|[basketId](#schemabasketid)|true|This identification of the corresponding signing basket object.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding http request IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Start the authorisation process for a signing basket

<a id="opIdstartSigningBasketAuthorisation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/signing-baskets/1234-basket-567/authorisations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -d 'null'
```

`POST /v1/signing-baskets/{basketId}/authorisations`

Create an authorisation sub-resource and start the authorisation process of a signing basket.
The message might in addition transmit authentication and authorisation related data.

This method is iterated n times for a n times SCA authorisation in a
corporate context, each creating an own authorisation sub-endpoint for
the corresponding PSU authorising the signing-baskets.

The ASPSP might make the usage of this access method unnecessary in case
of only one SCA process needed, since the related authorisation resource
might be automatically created by the ASPSP after the submission of the
payment data with the first POST signing basket call.

The start authorisation process is a process which is needed for creating a new authorisation
or cancellation sub-resource.

This applies in the following scenarios:

  * The ASPSP has indicated with a 'startAuthorisation' hyperlink in the preceding payment 
    initiation response that an explicit start of the authorisation process is needed by the TPP. 
    The 'startAuthorisation' hyperlink can transport more information about data which needs to be 
    uploaded by using the extended forms:
    * 'startAuthorisationWithPsuIdentfication', 
    * 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication' 
    * 'startAuthorisationWithEncryptedPsuAuthentication'
    * 'startAuthorisationWithAuthentciationMethodSelection'
  * The related payment initiation cannot yet be executed since a multilevel SCA is mandated.
  * The ASPSP has indicated with a 'startAuthorisation' hyperlink in the preceding 
    payment cancellation response that an explicit start of the authorisation process is needed by the TPP.
    The 'startAuthorisation' hyperlink can transport more information about data which needs to be uploaded
    by using the extended forms as indicated above.
  * The related payment cancellation request cannot be applied yet since a multilevel SCA is mandate for
    executing the cancellation.
  * The signing basket needs to be authorised yet.


> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="start-the-authorisation-process-for-a-signing-basket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|basketId|path|[basketId](#schemabasketid)|true|This identification of the corresponding signing basket object.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-ID|header|string|false|Client ID of the PSU in the ASPSP client interface.<br><br>Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation.<br><br>It might be contained even if an OAuth2 based authentication was performed in a pre-step or an OAuth2 based SCA was performed in an preceding<br>AIS service in the same session.<br>In this case the ASPSP might check whether PSU-ID and token match,<br>according to ASPSP documentation.<br>|
|PSU-ID-Type|header|string|false|Type of the PSU-ID, needed in scenarios where PSUs have several PSU-IDs as access possibility.<br><br>In this case, the mean and use are then defined in the ASPSP's documentation.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID-Type|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|TPP-Redirect-Preferred|header|boolean|false|If it equals "true", the TPP prefers a redirect over an embedded SCA approach.<br>If it equals "false", the TPP prefers not to be redirected for SCA. The ASPSP will then choose between the Embedded or the Decoupled<br>SCA approach, depending on the choice of the SCA procedure by the TPP/PSU.<br>If the parameter is not used, the ASPSP will choose the SCA approach to be applied depending on the SCA method chosen by the<br>TPP/PSU.<br>|
|TPP-Redirect-URI|header|string(uri)|false|URI of the TPP, where the transaction flow shall be redirected to after a Redirect.<br><br>Mandated for the Redirect SCA Approach, specifically<br>when TPP-Redirect-Preferred equals "true".<br>It is recommended to always use this header field.<br><br>**Remark for Future:**<br>This field might be changed to mandatory in the next version of the specification.<br>|
|TPP-Nok-Redirect-URI|header|string(uri)|false|If this URI is contained, the TPP is asking to redirect the transaction flow to this address instead of the TPP-Redirect-URI in case<br>of a negative result of the redirect SCA method. This might be ignored by the ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Notification-URI|header|string|false|URI for the Endpoint of the TPP-API to which the status of the payment initiation should be sent.<br>This header field may by ignored by the ASPSP.<br><br>For security reasons, it shall be ensured that the TPP-Notification-URI as introduced above is secured by the TPP eIDAS QWAC used for identification of the TPP. The following applies:<br><br>URIs which are provided by TPPs in TPP-Notification-URI shall comply with the domain secured by the eIDAS QWAC certificate of the TPP in the field CN or SubjectAltName of the certificate. Please note that in case of example-TPP.com as certificate entry TPP- Notification-URI like www.example-TPP.com/xs2a-client/v1/ASPSPidentifcation/mytransaction- id/notifications or notifications.example-TPP.com/xs2a-client/v1/ASPSPidentifcation/mytransaction- id/notifications would be compliant.<br><br>Wildcard definitions shall be taken into account for compliance checks by the ASPSP.<br> ASPSPs may respond with ASPSP-Notification-Support set to false, if the provided URIs do not comply.<br>|
|TPP-Notification-Content-Preferred|header|string|false|The string has the form<br><br>status=X1, ..., Xn<br><br>where Xi is one of the constants SCA, PROCESS, LAST and where constants are not<br>repeated.<br>The usage of the constants supports the of following semantics:<br><br>  SCA: A notification on every change of the scaStatus attribute for all related authorisation processes is preferred by the TPP.<br><br>  PROCESS: A notification on all changes of consentStatus or transactionStatus attributes is preferred by the TPP.<br>  LAST: Only a notification on the last consentStatus or transactionStatus as available in the XS2A interface is preferred by the TPP.<br><br>This header field may be ignored, if the ASPSP does not support resource notification services for the related TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding http request IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|
|body|body|object \| [updatePsuAuthentication](#schemaupdatepsuauthentication) \| [selectPsuAuthenticationMethod](#schemaselectpsuauthenticationmethod) \| [transactionAuthorisation](#schematransactionauthorisation)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[updatePsuAuthentication](#schemaupdatepsuauthentication)|false|Content of the body of a Update PSU authentication request<br><br>Password subfield is used.<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[selectPsuAuthenticationMethod](#schemaselectpsuauthenticationmethod)|false|Content of the body of a Select PSU authentication method request<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[transactionAuthorisation](#schematransactionauthorisation)|false|Content of the body of a transaction authorisation request<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

## Read the SCA status of the signing basket authorisation

<a id="opIdgetSigningBasketScaStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/signing-baskets/1234-basket-567/authorisations/123auth456 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721'
```

`GET /v1/signing-baskets/{basketId}/authorisations/{authorisationId}`

This method returns the SCA status of a signing basket's authorisation sub-resource.


<h3 id="read-the-sca-status-of-the-signing-basket-authorisation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|basketId|path|[basketId](#schemabasketid)|true|This identification of the corresponding signing basket object.<br>|
|authorisationId|path|[authorisationId](#schemaauthorisationid)|true|Resource identification of the related SCA.|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding http request IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

<h3 id="read-the-sca-status-of-the-signing-basket-authorisation-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[scaStatusResponse](#schemascastatusresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[Error400_NG_SBS](#schemaerror400_ng_sbs)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[Error401_NG_SBS](#schemaerror401_ng_sbs)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[Error403_NG_SBS](#schemaerror403_ng_sbs)|
|404|Not Found|Not found|[Error404_NG_SBS](#schemaerror404_ng_sbs)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method Not Allowed|[Error405_NG_SBS](#schemaerror405_ng_sbs)|
|406|Not Acceptable|Not Acceptable|None|
|408|Request Timeout|Request Timeout|None|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|[Error409_NG_SBS](#schemaerror409_ng_sbs)|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported Media Type|None|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too Many Requests|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error|None|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service Unavailable|None|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-Request-ID|string||ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|400|Location|string||Location of the created resource.<br>|

## Update PSU data for signing basket

<a id="opIdupdateSigningBasketPsuData"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/signing-baskets/1234-basket-567/authorisations/123auth456 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721' \
  -d '{
    "confirmationCode": "2256ffgh"
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/signing-baskets/{basketId}/authorisations/{authorisationId}`

This method update PSU data on the signing basket resource if needed. 
It may authorise a igning basket within the embedded SCA approach where needed.

Independently from the SCA Approach it supports e.g. the selection of 
the authentication method and a non-SCA PSU authentication.

There are several possible update PSU data requests in the context of a consent request if needed, 
which depends on the SCA approach:

* Redirect SCA Approach:
  A specific Update PSU data request is applicable for 
    * the selection of authentication methods, before choosing the actual SCA approach.
* Decoupled SCA Approach:
  A specific Update PSU data request is only applicable for
  * adding the PSU Identification, if not provided yet in the payment initiation request or the account information consent request, or if no OAuth2 access token is used, or
  * the selection of authentication methods.
* Embedded SCA Approach: 
  The update PSU data request might be used 
  * to add credentials as a first factor authentication data of the PSU and
  * to select the authentication method and
  * transaction authorisation.

The SCA approach might depend on the chosen SCA method. 
For that reason, the following possible update PSU data request can apply to all SCA approaches:

* Select an SCA method in case of several SCA methods are available for the customer.

There are the following request types on this access path:
  * Update PSU identification
  * Update PSU authentication
  * Select PSU autorization Method 
    WARNING: This method needs a reduced header, 
    therefore many optional elements are not present. 
    Maybe in a later version the access path will change.
  * Transaction Authorisation
    WARNING: This method needs a reduced header, 
    therefore many optional elements are not present. 
    Maybe in a later version the access path will change.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "confirmationCode": "2256ffgh"
}
```

<h3 id="update-psu-data-for-signing-basket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|basketId|path|[basketId](#schemabasketid)|true|This identification of the corresponding signing basket object.<br>|
|authorisationId|path|[authorisationId](#schemaauthorisationid)|true|Resource identification of the related SCA.|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-ID|header|string|false|Client ID of the PSU in the ASPSP client interface.<br><br>Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation.<br><br>It might be contained even if an OAuth2 based authentication was performed in a pre-step or an OAuth2 based SCA was performed in an preceding<br>AIS service in the same session.<br>In this case the ASPSP might check whether PSU-ID and token match,<br>according to ASPSP documentation.<br>|
|PSU-ID-Type|header|string|false|Type of the PSU-ID, needed in scenarios where PSUs have several PSU-IDs as access possibility.<br><br>In this case, the mean and use are then defined in the ASPSP's documentation.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID-Type|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding http request IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|
|body|body|object \| [updatePsuAuthentication](#schemaupdatepsuauthentication) \| [selectPsuAuthenticationMethod](#schemaselectpsuauthenticationmethod) \| [transactionAuthorisation](#schematransactionauthorisation) \| [authorisationConfirmation](#schemaauthorisationconfirmation)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[updatePsuAuthentication](#schemaupdatepsuauthentication)|false|Content of the body of a Update PSU authentication request<br><br>Password subfield is used.<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[selectPsuAuthenticationMethod](#schemaselectpsuauthenticationmethod)|false|Content of the body of a Select PSU authentication method request<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[transactionAuthorisation](#schematransactionauthorisation)|false|Content of the body of a transaction authorisation request<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[authorisationConfirmation](#schemaauthorisationconfirmation)|false|Content of the body of an authorisation confirmation request<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error|None|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service Unavailable|None|

<h3 id="update-psu-data-for-signing-basket-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[updatePsuIdenticationResponse](#schemaupdatepsuidenticationresponse)|false|none|Body of the JSON response for a successful update PSU identification request.|
|*oneOf*|[updatePsuAuthenticationResponse](#schemaupdatepsuauthenticationresponse)|false|none|Body of the JSON response for a successful update PSU authentication request.|
|*oneOf*|[selectPsuAuthenticationMethodResponse](#schemaselectpsuauthenticationmethodresponse)|false|none|Body of the JSON response for a successful select PSU authentication method request.|
|*oneOf*|[scaStatusResponse](#schemascastatusresponse)|false|none|Body of the JSON response with SCA Status.|
|*oneOf*|[authorisationConfirmationResponse](#schemaauthorisationconfirmationresponse)|false|none|Body of the JSON response for an authorisation confirmation request.|

## Read the status of the signing basket

<a id="opIdgetSigningBasketStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/signing-baskets/1234-basket-567/status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: 99391c7e-ad88-49ec-a2ad-99ddcb1f7721'
```

`GET /v1/signing-baskets/{basketId}/status`

Returns the status of a signing basket object.


<h3 id="read-the-status-of-the-signing-basket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|basketId|path|[basketId](#schemabasketid)|true|This identification of the corresponding signing basket object.<br>|
|X-Request-ID|header|string|true|ID of the request, unique to the call, as determined by the initiating party.|
|Digest|header|string|false|Is contained if and only if the "Signature" element is contained in the header of the request.|
|Signature|header|string|false|A signature of the request by the TPP on application level. This might be mandated by ASPSP.<br>|
|TPP-Signature-Certificate|header|string(byte)|false|The certificate used for signing the request, in base64 encoding.<br>Must be contained if a signature is contained.<br>|
|PSU-ID|header|string|false|Client ID of the PSU in the ASPSP client interface.<br><br>Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation.<br><br>It might be contained even if an OAuth2 based authentication was performed in a pre-step or an OAuth2 based SCA was performed in an preceding<br>AIS service in the same session.<br>In this case the ASPSP might check whether PSU-ID and token match,<br>according to ASPSP documentation.<br>|
|PSU-ID-Type|header|string|false|Type of the PSU-ID, needed in scenarios where PSUs have several PSU-IDs as access possibility.<br><br>In this case, the mean and use are then defined in the ASPSP's documentation.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|PSU-Corporate-ID-Type|header|string|false|Might be mandated in the ASPSP's documentation. Only used in a corporate context.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Address|header|string(ipv4)|false|The forwarded IP Address header field consists of the corresponding http request IP Address field between PSU and TPP.<br>|
|PSU-IP-Port|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Port header field consists of the corresponding HTTP request IP Port field between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Charset|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Accept-Language|header|string|false|The forwarded IP Accept header fields consist of the corresponding HTTP request Accept header fields between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-User-Agent|header|string|false|The forwarded Agent header field of the HTTP request between PSU and TPP, if available.<br>|
|PSU-Http-Method|header|string|false|HTTP method used at the PSU ? TPP interface, if available.<br>Valid values are:<br>* GET<br>* POST<br>* PUT<br>* PATCH<br>* DELETE<br>|
|PSU-Device-ID|header|string|false|UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) for a device, which is used by the PSU, if available.<br>UUID identifies either a device or a device dependant application installation.<br>In case of an installation identification this ID needs to be unaltered until removal from device.<br>|
|PSU-Geo-Location|header|string|false|The forwarded Geo Location of the corresponding http request between PSU and TPP if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|PSU-Http-Method|GET|
|PSU-Http-Method|POST|
|PSU-Http-Method|PUT|
|PSU-Http-Method|PATCH|
|PSU-Http-Method|DELETE|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|checkId|string|false|none|Identification of a Cheque.|
|creditorAccount|[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)|false|none|Reference to an account by either<br>  * IBAN, of a payment accounts, or<br>  * otherAccountIdentification, for payment accounts if there is no IBAN<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 CashAccount16-CH_IdTpCcy<br>|
|creditorAgent|[bicfi](#schemabicfi)|false|none|BICFI<br>|
|creditorId|[creditorId](#schemacreditorid)|false|none|Identification of Creditors, e.g. a SEPA Creditor ID.|
|creditorName|[creditorName](#schemacreditorname)|false|none|Creditor name.|
|currencyExchange|[reportExchangeRateList](#schemareportexchangeratelist)|false|none|Array of exchange rates.|
|debtorAccount|[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)|false|none|Reference to an account by either<br>  * IBAN, of a payment accounts, or<br>  * otherAccountIdentification, for payment accounts if there is no IBAN<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 CashAccount16-CH_IdTpCcy<br>|
|debtorAgent|[bicfi](#schemabicfi)|false|none|BICFI<br>|
|debtorName|[debtorName](#schemadebtorname)|false|none|Debtor name.|
|endToEndId|string|false|none|Unique end to end identity.|

Standardised definition of reporting error information according to [RFC7807]
in case of a HTTP error code 400 for AIS.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksAll](#schema_linksall)|false|none|A _link object with all availabel link types.<br>|
|additionalErrors|[object]|false|none|Array of Error Information Blocks.<br><br>Might be used if more than one error is to be communicated<br>|
|code|[MessageCode400_AIS](#schemamessagecode400_ais)|true|none|Message codes defined for AIS for HTTP Error code 400 (BAD_REQUEST).|
|detail|string|false|none|Detailed human readable text specific to this instance of the error.<br>XPath might be used to point to the issue generating the error in addition.<br>Remark for Future: In future, a dedicated field might be introduced for the XPath.<br>|
|title|string|false|none|Short human readable description of error type.<br>Could be in local language.<br>To be provided by ASPSPs.<br>|
|type|string(uri)|true|none|A URI reference [RFC3986] that identifies the problem type.<br>Remark For Future: These URI will be provided by NextGen in future.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|FORMAT_ERROR|
|code|PARAMETER_NOT_CONSISTENT|
|code|PARAMETER_NOT_SUPPORTED|
|code|SERVICE_INVALID|
|code|RESOURCE_UNKNOWN|
|code|RESOURCE_EXPIRED|
|code|RESOURCE_BLOCKED|
|code|TIMESTAMP_INVALID|
|code|PERIOD_INVALID|
|code|SCA_METHOD_UNKNOWN|
|code|SCA_INVALID|
|code|CONSENT_UNKNOWN|
|code|SESSIONS_NOT_SUPPORTED|

Standardised definition of reporting error information according to [RFC7807]
in case of a HTTP error code 400 for PIIS.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksAll](#schema_linksall)|false|none|A _link object with all availabel link types.<br>|
|additionalErrors|[object]|false|none|Array of Error Information Blocks.<br><br>Might be used if more than one error is to be communicated<br>|
|code|[MessageCode400_PIIS](#schemamessagecode400_piis)|true|none|Message codes defined for PIIS for HTTP Error code 400 (BAD_REQUEST).|
|detail|string|false|none|Detailed human readable text specific to this instance of the error.<br>XPath might be used to point to the issue generating the error in addition.<br>Remark for Future: In future, a dedicated field might be introduced for the XPath.<br>|
|title|string|false|none|Short human readable description of error type.<br>Could be in local language.<br>To be provided by ASPSPs.<br>|
|type|string(uri)|true|none|A URI reference [RFC3986] that identifies the problem type.<br>Remark For Future: These URI will be provided by NextGen in future.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|FORMAT_ERROR|
|code|PARAMETER_NOT_CONSISTENT|
|code|PARAMETER_NOT_SUPPORTED|
|code|SERVICE_INVALID|
|code|RESOURCE_UNKNOWN|
|code|RESOURCE_EXPIRED|
|code|RESOURCE_BLOCKED|
|code|TIMESTAMP_INVALID|
|code|PERIOD_INVALID|
|code|SCA_METHOD_UNKNOWN|
|code|SCA_INVALID|
|code|CONSENT_UNKNOWN|
|code|CARD_INVALID|
|code|NO_PIIS_ACTIVATION|

in case of a HTTP error code 401 for PIIS.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksAll](#schema_linksall)|false|none|A _link object with all availabel link types.<br>|
|additionalErrors|[object]|false|none|Array of Error Information Blocks.<br><br>Might be used if more than one error is to be communicated<br>|
|code|[MessageCode401_PIS](#schemamessagecode401_pis)|true|none|Message codes defined for PIS for HTTP Error code 401 (UNAUTHORIZED).|
|detail|string|false|none|Detailed human readable text specific to this instance of the error.<br>XPath might be used to point to the issue generating the error in addition.<br>Remark for Future: In future, a dedicated field might be introduced for the XPath.<br>|
|title|string|false|none|Short human readable description of error type.<br>Could be in local language.<br>To be provided by ASPSPs.<br>|
|type|string(uri)|true|none|A URI reference [RFC3986] that identifies the problem type.<br>Remark For Future: These URI will be provided by NextGen in future.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|CERTIFICATE_INVALID|
|code|ROLE_INVALID|
|code|CERTIFICATE_EXPIRED|
|code|CERTIFICATE_BLOCKED|
|code|CERTIFICATE_REVOKE|
|code|CERTIFICATE_MISSING|
|code|SIGNATURE_INVALID|
|code|SIGNATURE_MISSING|
|code|CORPORATE_ID_INVALID|
|code|PSU_CREDENTIALS_INVALID|
|code|CONSENT_INVALID|
|code|CONSENT_EXPIRED|
|code|TOKEN_UNKNOWN|
|code|TOKEN_INVALID|
|code|TOKEN_EXPIRED|
|code|REQUIRED_KID_MISSING|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|code|[MessageCode401_SBS](#schemamessagecode401_sbs)|true|none|Message codes defined for signing baskets for HTTP Error code 401 (UNAUTHORIZED).|
|detail|string|false|none|Detailed human readable text specific to this instance of the error.<br>XPath might be used to point to the issue generating the error in addition.<br>Remark for Future: In future, a dedicated field might be introduced for the XPath.<br>|
|title|string|false|none|Short human readable description of error type.<br>Could be in local language.<br>To be provided by ASPSPs.<br>|
|type|string(uri)|true|none|A URI reference [RFC3986] that identifies the problem type.<br>Remark For Future: These URI will be provided by NextGen in future.<br>|

|---|---|

|code|CONSENT_INVALID|
|code|CONSENT_EXPIRED|
|code|TOKEN_UNKNOWN|
|code|TOKEN_INVALID|
|code|TOKEN_EXPIRED|
