Standardised definition of reporting error information according to [RFC7807]
in case of a HTTP error code 403 for PIIS.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksAll](#schema_linksall)|false|none|A _link object with all availabel link types.<br>|
|additionalErrors|[object]|false|none|Array of Error Information Blocks.<br><br>Might be used if more than one error is to be communicated<br>|
|code|[MessageCode403_PIIS](#schemamessagecode403_piis)|true|none|Message codes defined for PIIS for HTTP Error code 403 (FORBIDDEN).|
|detail|string|false|none|Detailed human readable text specific to this instance of the error.<br>XPath might be used to point to the issue generating the error in addition.<br>Remark for Future: In future, a dedicated field might be introduced for the XPath.<br>|
|title|string|false|none|Short human readable description of error type.<br>Could be in local language.<br>To be provided by ASPSPs.<br>|
|type|string(uri)|true|none|A URI reference [RFC3986] that identifies the problem type.<br>Remark For Future: These URI will be provided by NextGen in future.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|CONSENT_UNKNOWN|
|code|SERVICE_BLOCKED|
|code|RESOURCE_UNKNOWN|
|code|RESOURCE_EXPIRED|

in case of a HTTP error code 403 for signing baskets.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksAll](#schema_linksall)|false|none|A _link object with all availabel link types.<br>|
|additionalErrors|[object]|false|none|Array of Error Information Blocks.<br><br>Might be used if more than one error is to be communicated<br>|
|code|[MessageCode403_SBS](#schemamessagecode403_sbs)|true|none|Message codes defined for signing baskets for HTTP Error code 403 (FORBIDDEN).|
|detail|string|false|none|Detailed human readable text specific to this instance of the error.<br>XPath might be used to point to the issue generating the error in addition.<br>Remark for Future: In future, a dedicated field might be introduced for the XPath.<br>|
|title|string|false|none|Short human readable description of error type.<br>Could be in local language.<br>To be provided by ASPSPs.<br>|
|type|string(uri)|true|none|A URI reference [RFC3986] that identifies the problem type.<br>Remark For Future: These URI will be provided by NextGen in future.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|CONSENT_UNKNOWN|
|code|SERVICE_BLOCKED|
|code|RESOURCE_UNKNOWN|
|code|RESOURCE_EXPIRED|

|code|[MessageCode404_PIIS](#schemamessagecode404_piis)|true|none|Message codes defined for PIIS for HTTP Error code 404 (NOT FOUND).|
|detail|string|false|none|Detailed human readable text specific to this instance of the error.<br>XPath might be used to point to the issue generating the error in addition.<br>Remark for Future: In future, a dedicated field might be introduced for the XPath.<br>|
|title|string|false|none|Short human readable description of error type.<br>Could be in local language.<br>To be provided by ASPSPs.<br>|
|type|string(uri)|true|none|A URI reference [RFC3986] that identifies the problem type.<br>Remark For Future: These URI will be provided by NextGen in future.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|RESOURCE_UNKNOWN|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|detail|string|false|none|Detailed human readable text specific to this instance of the error.<br>XPath might be used to point to the issue generating the error in addition.<br>Remark for Future: In future, a dedicated field might be introduced for the XPath.<br>|
|title|string|false|none|Short human readable description of error type.<br>Could be in local language.<br>To be provided by ASPSPs.<br>|
|type|string(uri)|true|none|A URI reference [RFC3986] that identifies the problem type.<br>Remark For Future: These URI will be provided by NextGen in future.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|RESOURCE_UNKNOWN|

Standardised definition of reporting error information according to [RFC7807]
in case of a HTTP error code 405 for PIIS.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksAll](#schema_linksall)|false|none|A _link object with all availabel link types.<br>|
|additionalErrors|[object]|false|none|Array of Error Information Blocks.<br><br>Might be used if more than one error is to be communicated<br>|
|code|[MessageCode405_PIIS](#schemamessagecode405_piis)|true|none|Message codes defined for PIIS for HTTP Error code 405 (METHOD NOT ALLOWED).|
|detail|string|false|none|Detailed human readable text specific to this instance of the error.<br>XPath might be used to point to the issue generating the error in addition.<br>Remark for Future: In future, a dedicated field might be introduced for the XPath.<br>|
|title|string|false|none|Short human readable description of error type.<br>Could be in local language.<br>To be provided by ASPSPs.<br>|
|type|string(uri)|true|none|A URI reference [RFC3986] that identifies the problem type.<br>Remark For Future: These URI will be provided by NextGen in future.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|SERVICE_INVALID|

in case of a HTTP error code 409 for AIS.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksAll](#schema_linksall)|false|none|A _link object with all availabel link types.<br>|
|additionalErrors|[object]|false|none|Array of Error Information Blocks.<br><br>Might be used if more than one error is to be communicated<br>|
|code|[MessageCode409_AIS](#schemamessagecode409_ais)|true|none|Message codes defined for AIS for HTTP Error code 409 (CONFLICT).|
|detail|string|false|none|Detailed human readable text specific to this instance of the error.<br>XPath might be used to point to the issue generating the error in addition.<br>Remark for Future: In future, a dedicated field might be introduced for the XPath.<br>|
|title|string|false|none|Short human readable description of error type.<br>Could be in local language.<br>To be provided by ASPSPs.<br>|
|type|string(uri)|true|none|A URI reference [RFC3986] that identifies the problem type.<br>Remark For Future: These URI will be provided by NextGen in future.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|STATUS_INVALID|

```json
  },
  "property2": {
    "href": "/v1/payments/swiss-sepa-credit-transfers/1234-wertiq-983"
  }
}
```

A list of hyperlinks to be recognised by the TPP.

Type of links admitted in this response (which might be extended by single ASPSPs as indicated in its XS2A
documentation):
  * 'scaRedirect': 
    In case of an SCA Redirect Approach, the ASPSP is transmitting the link to which to redirect the 
    PSU browser.
  * 'scaOAuth': 
    In case of an OAuth2 based Redirect Approach, the ASPSP is transmitting the link where the configuration 
    of the OAuth2 Server is defined. 
    The configuration follows the OAuth 2.0 Authorisation Server Metadata specification. 
* 'confirmation': 
  Might be added by the ASPSP if either the "scaRedirect" or "scaOAuth" hyperlink is returned 
  in the same response message. 
  This hyperlink defines the URL to the resource which needs to be updated with 
    * a confirmation code as retrieved after the plain redirect authentication process with the ASPSP authentication server or
    * an access token as retrieved by submitting an authorization code after the integrated OAuth based authentication process with the ASPSP authentication server.
  * 'startAuthorisation': 
    In case, where an explicit start of the transaction authorisation is needed, 
    but no more data needs to be updated (no authentication method to be selected, 
    no PSU identification nor PSU authentication data to be uploaded).
  * 'startAuthorisationWithPsuIdentification': 
    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated 
    while uploading the PSU identification data.
  * 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication':
    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated 
    while uploading the PSU authentication data.
  * 'startAuthorisationWithEncryptedPsuAuthentication':
    Same as startAuthorisactionWithPsuAuthentication where the authentication data need to be encrypted on
    application layer in uploading.
  * 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection':
    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated 
    while selecting the authentication method. This link is contained under exactly the same conditions 
    as the data element 'scaMethods' 
  * 'startAuthorisationWithTransactionAuthorisation':
    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated 
    while authorising the transaction e.g. by uploading an OTP received by SMS.
  * 'self': 
    The link to the Establish Account Information Consent resource created by this request. 
    This link can be used to retrieve the resource data. 
  * 'status': 
    The link to retrieve the status of the account information consent.
  * 'scaStatus': The link to retrieve the scaStatus of the corresponding authorisation sub-resource. 
    This link is only contained, if an authorisation sub-resource has been already created.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|confirmation|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|scaOAuth|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|scaRedirect|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|scaStatus|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|self|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|startAuthorisation|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|startAuthorisationWithEncryptedPsuAuthentication|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|startAuthorisationWithPsuIdentification|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|startAuthorisationWithTransactionAuthorisation|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|status|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|**additionalProperties**|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|

Type of links admitted in this response, (further links might be added for ASPSP defined extensions):

* 'scaRedirect':
  In case of an SCA Redirect Approach, the ASPSP is transmitting the link to which to redirect the PSU browser.
* 'scaOAuth':
  In case of a SCA OAuth2 Approach, the ASPSP is transmitting the URI where the configuration of the Authorisation
  Server can be retrieved. The configuration follows the OAuth 2.0 Authorisation Server Metadata specification.
* 'confirmation': 
  Might be added by the ASPSP if either the "scaRedirect" or "scaOAuth" hyperlink is returned 
  in the same response message. 
  This hyperlink defines the URL to the resource which needs to be updated with 
    * a confirmation code as retrieved after the plain redirect authentication process with the ASPSP authentication server or
    * an access token as retrieved by submitting an authorization code after the integrated OAuth based authentication process with the ASPSP authentication server. 
* 'startAuthorisation': 
  In case, where an explicit start of the transaction authorisation is needed, but no more data needs to be updated 
  (no authentication method to be selected, no PSU identification nor PSU authentication data to be uploaded).
* 'startAuthorisationWithPsuIdentification':
  The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated while
  uploading the PSU identification data.
* 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication':
  The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated while
  uploading the PSU authentication data.
  * 'startAuthorisationWithEncryptedPsuAuthentication':
    Same as startAuthorisactionWithPsuAuthentication where the authentication data need to be encrypted on
    application layer in uploading.
* 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection':
  The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated while
  selecting the authentication method.
  This link is contained under exactly the same conditions as the data element "scaMethods"
* 'startAuthorisationWithTransactionAuthorisation':
  The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated while
  authorising the transaction e.g. by uploading an OTP received by SMS.
* 'self':
  The link to the payment initiation resource created by this request.
  This link can be used to retrieve the resource data.
* 'status':
  The link to retrieve the transaction status of the payment initiation.
* 'scaStatus':
  The link to retrieve the scaStatus of the corresponding authorisation sub-resource.
  This link is only contained, if an authorisation sub-resource has been already created.

Remark: All links can be relative or full links, to be decided by the ASPSP.

    application layer in uploading.
  * 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection':
    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the cancellation-authorisation sub-resource has to be
    generated while selecting the authentication method. This link is contained under exactly the same
    conditions as the data element 'scaMethods'

A list of hyperlinks to be recognised by the TPP. Might be contained, if several authentication methods
are available for the PSU.
Type of links admitted in this response:
  * 'updateAdditionalPsuAuthentication':
    The link to the payment initiation or account information resource,
    which needs to be updated by an additional PSU password.
    This link is only contained in rare cases,
    where such additional passwords are needed for PSU authentications.
  * 'updateAdditionalEncryptedPsuAuthentication':
    The link to the payment initiation or account information resource,
    which needs to be updated by an additional encrypted PSU password.
    This link is only contained in rare cases, where such additional passwords are needed for PSU authentications.
  * 'selectAuthenticationMethod':
    This is a link to a resource, where the TPP can select the applicable second factor authentication
    methods for the PSU, if there were several available authentication methods.
    This link is only contained, if the PSU is already identified or authenticated with the first relevant
    factor or alternatively an access token, if SCA is required and if the PSU has a choice between different
    authentication methods.
    If this link is contained, then there is also the data element 'scaMethods' contained in the response body.
  * 'authoriseTransaction': 
    The link to the resource, where the "Transaction authorisation request" is sent to. 
    This is the link to the resource which will authorise the transaction by checking the SCA authentication 
    data within the Embedded SCA approach.
  * 'scaStatus':
    The link to retrieve the scaStatus of the corresponding authorisation sub-resource.

```json
  },
  "selectAuthenticationMethod": {
    "href": "/v1/payments/swiss-sepa-credit-transfers/1234-wertiq-983"
  },
  "property1": {
    "href": "/v1/payments/swiss-sepa-credit-transfers/1234-wertiq-983"
  },
  "property2": {
    "href": "/v1/payments/swiss-sepa-credit-transfers/1234-wertiq-983"
  }
}
```

A list of hyperlinks to be recognised by the TPP. The actual hyperlinks used in the response depend on the dynamical decisions of the ASPSP when processing the request.

**Remark:** All links can be relative or full links, to be decided by the ASPSP.

Type of links admitted in this response, (further links might be added for ASPSP
defined extensions):

- 'scaStatus': The link to retrieve the scaStatus of the corresponding authorisation sub-resource.
- 'selectAuthenticationMethod': This is a link to a resource, where the TPP can select the applicable second factor authentication methods for the PSU, if there are several available authentication methods and if the PSU is already sufficiently authenticated.. If this link is contained, then there is also the data element "scaMethods" contained in the response body.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scaStatus|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|selectAuthenticationMethod|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|
|**additionalProperties**|[hrefType](#schemahreftype)|false|none|Link to a resource.|

Requested access services for a consent.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accounts|[[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)]|false|none|Is asking for detailed account information. <br><br>If the array is empty in a request, the TPP is asking for an accessible account list. <br>This may be restricted in a PSU/ASPSP authorization dialogue. <br>If the array is empty, also the arrays for balances, additionalInformation sub attributes or transactions shall be empty, if used.<br>|
|additionalInformation|[additionalInformationAccess](#schemaadditionalinformationaccess)|false|none|Optional if supported by API provider.<br><br>Is asking for additional information as added within this structured object.<br>The usage of this data element requires at least one of the entries "accounts", <br>"transactions" or "balances" also to be contained in the object. <br>If detailed accounts are referenced, it is required in addition that any account addressed within <br>the additionalInformation attribute is also addressed by at least one of the attributes "accounts", <br>"transactions" or "balances".<br>|
|allPsd2|string|false|none|Optional if supported by API provider.<br><br>The values "allAccounts" and "allAccountsWithOwnerName" are admitted. <br>The support of the "allAccountsWithOwnerName" value by the ASPSP is optional.<br>|
|availableAccounts|string|false|none|Optional if supported by API provider.<br><br>The values "allAccounts" and "allAccountsWithOwnerName" are admitted. <br>The support of the "allAccountsWithOwnerName" value by the ASPSP is optional.<br>|
|availableAccountsWithBalance|string|false|none|Optional if supported by API provider.<br><br>The values "allAccounts" and "allAccountsWithOwnerName" are admitted. <br>The support of the "allAccountsWithOwnerName" value by the ASPSP is optional.<br>|
|balances|[[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)]|false|none|Is asking for balances of the addressed accounts.<br><br>If the array is empty in the request, the TPP is asking for the balances of all accessible account lists. <br>This may be restricted in a PSU/ASPSP authorization dialogue. <br>If the array is empty, also the arrays for accounts, additionalInformation sub attributes or transactions shall be empty, if used.<br>|
|restrictedTo|[[cashAccountType](#schemacashaccounttype)]|false|none|If the TPP requests access to accounts via availableAccounts (List of available accounts), global <br>or bank driven consents, the TPP may include this element to restrict access to the referred <br>account types. Absence of the element is interpreted as "no restriction" (therefore access to <br>accounts of all types is requested). The element may only occur, if each of the elements <br>  - accounts <br>  - balances <br>  - transactions <br>is either not present or contains an empty array. <br>|
|transactions|[[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)]|false|none|Is asking for transactions of the addressed accounts. <br><br>If the array is empty in the request, the TPP is asking for the transactions of all accessible account lists. <br>This may be restricted in a PSU/ASPSP authorization dialogue. <br>If the array is empty, also the arrays for accounts, additionalInformation sub attributes or balances shall be empty, if used.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|allPsd2|allAccounts|
|allPsd2|allAccountsWithOwnerName|
|availableAccounts|allAccounts|
|availableAccounts|allAccountsWithOwnerName|
|availableAccountsWithBalance|allAccounts|
|availableAccountsWithBalance|allAccountsWithOwnerName|

The ASPSP shall give at least one of the account reference identifiers:
  - iban
  - bban
  - pan
  - maskedPan
  - msisdn
If the account is a multicurrency account currency code in "currency" is set to "XXX".

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksAccountDetails](#schema_linksaccountdetails)|false|none|Links to the account, which can be directly used for retrieving account information from this dedicated account.<br><br>Links to "balances" and/or "transactions"<br><br>These links are only supported, when the corresponding consent has been already granted.<br>|
|balances|[balanceList](#schemabalancelist)|false|none|A list of balances regarding this account, e.g. the current balance, the last booked balance.<br>The list might be restricted to the current balance.<br>|
|bban|[bban](#schemabban)|false|none|Basic Bank Account Number (BBAN) Identifier.<br><br>This data element can be used in the body of the consent request.<br>  Message for retrieving account access consent from this account. This<br>  data elements is used for payment accounts which have no IBAN.<br>  ISO20022: Basic Bank Account Number (BBAN). <br>  <br>  Identifier used nationally by financial institutions, i.e., in individual countries, <br>  generally as part of a National Account Numbering Scheme(s), <br>  which uniquely identifies the account of a customer.<br>|
|bic|[bicfi](#schemabicfi)|false|none|BICFI<br>|
|cashAccountType|[cashAccountType](#schemacashaccounttype)|false|none|ExternalCashAccountType1Code from ISO 20022.<br>|
|currency|[currencyCode](#schemacurrencycode)|true|none|ISO 4217 Alpha 3 currency code.<br>|
|details|string|false|none|Specifications that might be provided by the ASPSP:<br>  - characteristics of the account<br>  - characteristics of the relevant card<br>|
|displayName|[displayName](#schemadisplayname)|false|none|Name of the account as defined by the PSU within online channels.<br>|
|iban|[iban](#schemaiban)|false|none|IBAN of an account.|
|linkedAccounts|string|false|none|Case of a set of pending card transactions, the APSP will provide the relevant cash account the card is set up on.|
|msisdn|[msisdn](#schemamsisdn)|false|none|Mobile phone number.|
|name|string|false|none|Name of the account, as assigned by the ASPSP, in agreement with the account owner in order to provide an additional means of identification of the account.|
|ownerName|[ownerName](#schemaownername)|false|none|Name of the legal account owner. <br>If there is more than one owner, then e.g. two names might be noted here.<br><br>For a corporate account, the corporate name is used for this attribute.<br>Even if supported by the ASPSP, the provision of this field might depend on the fact whether an explicit consent to this specific additional account information has been given by the PSU.<br>|
|product|string|false|none|Product name of the bank for this account, proprietary definition.|
|resourceId|string|false|none|This shall be filled, if addressable resource are created by the ASPSP on the /accounts or /card-accounts endpoint.|
|status|[accountStatus](#schemaaccountstatus)|false|none|Account status. The value is one of the following:<br>  - "enabled": account is available<br>  - "deleted": account is terminated<br>  - "blocked": account is blocked e.g. for legal reasons<br>If this field is not used, than the account is available in the sense of this specification.<br>|
|usage|string|false|none|Specifies the usage of the account:<br>  * PRIV: private personal account<br>  * ORGA: professional account<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|enabled|
|status|deleted|
|status|blocked|
|usage|PRIV|
|usage|ORGA|

JSON based account report.
This account report contains transactions resulting from the query parameters.

'booked' shall be contained if bookingStatus parameter is set to "booked" or "both".

'pending' is not contained if the bookingStatus parameter is set to "booked" or "information".

'information' Only contained if the bookingStatus is set to "information" and if supported by ASPSP.

|_links|[_linksAccountReport](#schema_linksaccountreport)|true|none|none|
|booked|[transactionList](#schematransactionlist)|false|none|Array of transaction details.|
|information|[transactionList](#schematransactionlist)|false|none|Array of transaction details.|
|pending|[transactionList](#schematransactionlist)|false|none|Array of transaction details.|

<h2 id="tocS_accountStatus">accountStatus</h2>

```json
"enabled"
```

Account status. The value is one of the following:
  - "enabled": account is available
  - "deleted": account is terminated
  - "blocked": account is blocked e.g. for legal reasons
If this field is not used, than the account is available in the sense of this specification.

```json
{
  "ownerName": [
    {
      "cashAccountType": "string",
      "currency": "EUR",
      "iban": "FR7612345987650123456789014",
      "otherAccountIdentification": "90-100100-0"
    }
  ],
  "trustedBeneficiaries": [
    {
      "cashAccountType": "string",
      "currency": "EUR",
      "iban": "FR7612345987650123456789014",
      "otherAccountIdentification": "90-100100-0"
    }
  ]

```

Optional if supported by API provider.

Is asking for additional information as added within this structured object.
The usage of this data element requires at least one of the entries "accounts", 
"transactions" or "balances" also to be contained in the object. 
If detailed accounts are referenced, it is required in addition that any account addressed within 
the additionalInformation attribute is also addressed by at least one of the attributes "accounts", 
"transactions" or "balances".

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ownerName|[[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)]|false|none|Is asking for account owner name of the accounts referenced within. <br>If the array is empty in the request, the TPP is asking for the account <br>owner name of all accessible accounts. <br>This may be restricted in a PSU/ASPSP authorization dialogue. <br>If the array is empty, also the arrays for accounts, balances or transactions shall be empty, if used.<br>The ASPSP will indicate in the consent resource after a successful authorisation, <br>whether the ownerName consent can be accepted by providing the accounts on which the ownerName will <br>be delivered. <br>This array can be empty.<br>|
|trustedBeneficiaries|[[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)]|false|none|Optional if supported by API provider.<br>Is asking for the trusted beneficiaries related to the accounts referenced within and related to the PSU.<br>If the array is empty in the request, the TPP is asking for the lists of trusted beneficiaries of all accessible accounts. <br>This may be restricted in a PSU/ASPSP authorization dialogue by the PSU if also the account lists addressed <br>by the tags “accounts”, “balances” or “transactions” are empty.<br>The ASPSP will indicate in the consent resource after a successful authorisation, <br>whether the trustedBeneficiaries consent can be accepted by providing the accounts on which the list of trusted beneficiaries will be delivered. <br>This array can be empty.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_authenticationObject">authenticationObject</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="tocsauthenticationobject"></a>

```json
{
  "authenticationMethodId": "myAuthenticationID",
  "authenticationType": "SMS_OTP",
  "authenticationVersion": "string",
  "explanation": "Detailed information about the SCA method for the PSU.",
  "name": "SMS OTP on phone +49160 xxxxx 28"
}
```

Authentication object.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authenticationMethodId|[authenticationMethodId](#schemaauthenticationmethodid)|true|none|An identification provided by the ASPSP for the later identification of the authentication method selection.<br>|
|authenticationType|[authenticationType](#schemaauthenticationtype)|true|none|Type of the authentication method.<br><br>More authentication types might be added during implementation projects and documented in the ASPSP documentation.<br><br>  - 'SMS_OTP': An SCA method, where an OTP linked to the transaction to be authorised is sent to the PSU through a SMS channel.<br>  - 'CHIP_OTP': An SCA method, where an OTP is generated by a chip card, e.g. a TOP derived from an EMV cryptogram. <br>    To contact the card, the PSU normally needs a (handheld) device. <br>    With this device, the PSU either reads the challenging data through a visual interface like flickering or <br>    the PSU types in the challenge through the device key pad. <br>    The device then derives an OTP from the challenge data and displays the OTP to the PSU.<br>  - 'PHOTO_OTP': An SCA method, where the challenge is a QR code or similar encoded visual data<br>    which can be read in by a consumer device or specific mobile app.<br>    The device resp. the specific app than derives an OTP from the visual challenge data and displays<br>    the OTP to the PSU.<br>  - 'PUSH_OTP': An OTP is pushed to a dedicated authentication APP and displayed to the PSU.<br>  - 'SMTP_OTP': An OTP is sent via email to the PSU.<br>|
|authenticationVersion|string|false|none|Depending on the "authenticationType".<br>This version can be used by differentiating authentication tools used within performing OTP generation in the same authentication type.<br>This version can be referred to in the ASPSP?s documentation.<br>|
|explanation|string|false|none|Detailed information about the SCA method for the PSU.<br>|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the authentication method defined by the PSU in the Online Banking frontend of the ASPSP.<br>Alternatively this could be a description provided by the ASPSP like "SMS OTP on phone +49160 xxxxx 28".<br>This name shall be used by the TPP when presenting a list of authentication methods to the PSU, if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|authenticationType|SMS_OTP|
|authenticationType|CHIP_OTP|
|authenticationType|PHOTO_OTP|
|authenticationType|PUSH_OTP|
|authenticationType|SMTP_OTP|

<h2 id="tocS_authenticationType">authenticationType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaauthenticationtype"></a>
<a id="schema_authenticationType"></a>
<a id="tocSauthenticationtype"></a>
<a id="tocsauthenticationtype"></a>

```json
"SMS_OTP"
```

Type of the authentication method.

More authentication types might be added during implementation projects and documented in the ASPSP documentation.

  - 'SMS_OTP': An SCA method, where an OTP linked to the transaction to be authorised is sent to the PSU through a SMS channel.
  - 'CHIP_OTP': An SCA method, where an OTP is generated by a chip card, e.g. a TOP derived from an EMV cryptogram. 
    To contact the card, the PSU normally needs a (handheld) device. 
    With this device, the PSU either reads the challenging data through a visual interface like flickering or 
    the PSU types in the challenge through the device key pad. 
    The device then derives an OTP from the challenge data and displays the OTP to the PSU.
  - 'PHOTO_OTP': An SCA method, where the challenge is a QR code or similar encoded visual data
    which can be read in by a consumer device or specific mobile app.
    The device resp. the specific app than derives an OTP from the visual challenge data and displays
    the OTP to the PSU.
  - 'PUSH_OTP': An OTP is pushed to a dedicated authentication APP and displayed to the PSU.
  - 'SMTP_OTP': An OTP is sent via email to the PSU.

```json

  },
  "balanceType": "closingBooked",

  "lastChangeDateTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
```

A single balance element.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|balanceAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|none|
|balanceType|[balanceType](#schemabalancetype)|true|none|The following balance types are defined:<br>  - "closingBooked":<br>    Balance of the account at the end of the pre-agreed account reporting period.<br>    It is the sum of the opening booked balance at the beginning of the period and all entries booked<br>    to the account during the pre-agreed account reporting period.<br><br>    For card-accounts, this is composed of<br><br>      - invoiced, but not yet paid entries<br><br>  - "expected":<br>    Balance composed of booked entries and pending items known at the time of calculation,<br>    which projects the end of day balance if everything is booked on the account and no other entry is posted.<br>    <br>    For card accounts, this is composed of:<br>      - invoiced, but not yet paid entries<br>      - not yet invoiced but already booked entries and<br>      - pending items (not yet booked)<br>    <br>    For card-accounts:<br><br>    "money to spend with the value of a pre-approved credit limit on the card account"<br><br>  - "openingBooked":<br>    Book balance of the account at the beginning of the account reporting period.<br>    It always equals the closing book balance from the previous report.<br>  - "interimAvailable":<br>    Available balance calculated in the course of the account ?servicer?s business day,<br>    at the time specified, and subject to further changes during the business day.<br>    The interim balance is calculated on the basis of booked credit and debit items during the calculation<br>    time/period specified.<br>    <br>    For card-accounts, this is composed of:<br>      - invoiced, but not yet paid entries<br>      - not yet invoiced but already booked entries<br>  - "interimBooked":<br>    Balance calculated in the course of the account servicer's business day, at the time specified,<br>    and subject to further changes during the business day.<br>    The interim balance is calculated on the basis of booked credit and debit items during the calculation time/period<br>    specified.<br>  - "forwardAvailable":<br>    Forward available balance of money that is at the disposal of the account owner on the date specified.<br>  - "nonInvoiced":<br>    Only for card accounts, to be checked yet.<br>|
|creditLimitIncluded|boolean|false|none|A flag indicating if the credit limit of the corresponding account<br>is included in the calculation of the balance, where applicable.<br>|
|lastChangeDateTime|string(date-time)|false|none|This data element might be used to indicate e.g. with the expected or booked balance that no action is known<br>on the account, which is not yet booked.<br>|
|lastCommittedTransaction|string|false|none|"entryReference" of the last commited transaction to support the TPP in identifying whether all<br>PSU transactions are already known.<br>|
|referenceDate|string(date)|false|none|Indicates the date of the balance.|

<h2 id="tocS_balanceType">balanceType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabalancetype"></a>
<a id="schema_balanceType"></a>
<a id="tocSbalancetype"></a>
<a id="tocsbalancetype"></a>

```json
"closingBooked"
```

The following balance types are defined:
  - "closingBooked":
    Balance of the account at the end of the pre-agreed account reporting period.
    It is the sum of the opening booked balance at the beginning of the period and all entries booked
    to the account during the pre-agreed account reporting period.

    For card-accounts, this is composed of

      - invoiced, but not yet paid entries

  - "expected":
    Balance composed of booked entries and pending items known at the time of calculation,
    which projects the end of day balance if everything is booked on the account and no other entry is posted.
    
    For card accounts, this is composed of:
      - invoiced, but not yet paid entries
      - not yet invoiced but already booked entries and
      - pending items (not yet booked)
    
    For card-accounts:

    "money to spend with the value of a pre-approved credit limit on the card account"

  - "openingBooked":
    Book balance of the account at the beginning of the account reporting period.
    It always equals the closing book balance from the previous report.
  - "interimAvailable":
    Available balance calculated in the course of the account ?servicer?s business day,
    at the time specified, and subject to further changes during the business day.
    The interim balance is calculated on the basis of booked credit and debit items during the calculation
    time/period specified.
    
    For card-accounts, this is composed of:
      - invoiced, but not yet paid entries
      - not yet invoiced but already booked entries
  - "interimBooked":
    Balance calculated in the course of the account servicer's business day, at the time specified,
    and subject to further changes during the business day.
    The interim balance is calculated on the basis of booked credit and debit items during the calculation time/period
    specified.
  - "forwardAvailable":
    Forward available balance of money that is at the disposal of the account owner on the date specified.
  - "nonInvoiced":
    Only for card accounts, to be checked yet.

<a id="tocsbanktransactioncode"></a>

```json
"PMNT-RDDT-ESDD"
```

Bank transaction code as used by the ASPSP and using the sub elements of this structured code defined by ISO 20022.

This code type is concatenating the three ISO20022 Codes
  * Domain Code,
  * Family Code, and
  * SubFamiliy Code
by hyphens, resulting in 'DomainCode'-'FamilyCode'-'SubFamilyCode'.

If this element equals 'true', the PSU prefers only one booking entry.
If this element equals 'false', the PSU prefers individual booking of all contained individual transactions.

The ASPSP will follow this preference according to contracts agreed on with the PSU.

This data element can be used in the body of the consent request.

  data elements is used for payment accounts which have no IBAN.
  ISO20022: Basic Bank Account Number (BBAN). 
  
  Identifier used nationally by financial institutions, i.e., in individual countries, 
  generally as part of a National Account Numbering Scheme(s), 
  which uniquely identifies the account of a customer.

Generic JSON response body consistion of the corresponding bulk payment initation JSON body together with an optional transaction status field.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acceptorTransactionDateTime|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|batchBookingPreferred|[batchBookingPreferred](#schemabatchbookingpreferred)|false|none|If this element equals 'true', the PSU prefers only one booking entry.<br>If this element equals 'false', the PSU prefers individual booking of all contained individual transactions.<br><br>The ASPSP will follow this preference according to contracts agreed on with the PSU.<br>|
|debtorAccount|[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)|true|none|Reference to an account by either<br>  * IBAN, of a payment accounts, or<br>  * otherAccountIdentification, for payment accounts if there is no IBAN<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 CashAccount16-CH_IdTpCcy<br>|
|paymentInformationId|string|false|none|none|
|payments|[[paymentInitiationBulkElement_json](#schemapaymentinitiationbulkelement_json)]|true|none|A list of generic JSON bodies payment initations for bulk payments via JSON.<br><br>Note: Some fields from single payments do not occcur in a bulk payment element<br>|
|requestedExecutionDate|string(date)|false|none|none|
|transactionStatus|[transactionStatus](#schematransactionstatus)|false|none|The transaction status is filled with codes of the ISO 20022 data table:<br>- 'ACCC': 'AcceptedSettlementCompleted' -<br>  Settlement on the creditor's account has been completed.<br>- 'ACCP': 'AcceptedCustomerProfile' -<br>  Preceding check of technical validation was successful.<br>  Customer profile check was also successful.<br>- 'ACSC': 'AcceptedSettlementCompleted' -<br>  Settlement on the debtoro?=s account has been completed.<br><br>  **Usage:** this can be used by the first agent to report to the debtor that the transaction has been completed.<br><br>  **Warning:** this status is provided for transaction status reasons, not for financial information.<br>  It can only be used after bilateral agreement.<br>- 'ACSP': 'AcceptedSettlementInProcess' -<br>  All preceding checks such as technical validation and customer profile were successful and therefore the payment initiation has been accepted for execution.<br>- 'ACTC': 'AcceptedTechnicalValidation' -<br>  Authentication and syntactical and semantical validation are successful.<br>- 'ACWC': 'AcceptedWithChange' -<br>  Instruction is accepted but a change will be made, such as date or remittance not sent.<br>- 'ACWP': 'AcceptedWithoutPosting' -<br>  Payment instruction included in the credit transfer is accepted without being posted to the creditor customero?=s account.<br>- 'RCVD': 'Received' -<br>  Payment initiation has been received by the receiving agent.<br>- 'PDNG': 'Pending' -<br>  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation is pending.<br>  Further checks and status update will be performed.<br>- 'RJCT': 'Rejected' -<br>  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation has been rejected.<br>- 'CANC': 'Cancelled'<br>  Payment initiation has been cancelled before execution<br>  Remark: This codeis accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'ACFC': 'AcceptedFundsChecked' -<br>  Preceding check of technical validation and customer profile was successful and an automatic funds check was positive .<br>  Remark: This code is accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'PATC': 'PartiallyAcceptedTechnical'<br>  Correct The payment initiation needs multiple authentications, where some but not yet all have been performed. Syntactical and semantical validations are successful.<br>  Remark: This code is accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'PART': 'PartiallyAccepted' -<br>  A number of transactions have been accepted, whereas another number of transactions have not yet achieved 'accepted' status.<br>  Remark: This code may be used only in case of bulk payments. It is only used in a situation where all mandated authorisations have been applied, but some payments have been rejected.<br>|

|status|[accountStatus](#schemaaccountstatus)|false|none|Account status. The value is one of the following:<br>  - "enabled": account is available<br>  - "deleted": account is terminated<br>  - "blocked": account is blocked e.g. for legal reasons<br>If this field is not used, than the account is available in the sense of this specification.<br>|

|balances|[balanceList](#schemabalancelist)|false|none|A list of balances regarding this account, e.g. the current balance, the last booked balance.<br>The list might be restricted to the current balance.<br>|
|cardAccount|[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)|false|none|Reference to an account by either<br>  * IBAN, of a payment accounts, or<br>  * otherAccountIdentification, for payment accounts if there is no IBAN<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 CashAccount16-CH_IdTpCcy<br>|
|cardTransactions|[cardAccountReport](#schemacardaccountreport)|false|none|JSON based card account report.<br><br>This card account report contains transactions resulting from the query parameters.<br>|
|debitAccounting|[debitAccounting](#schemadebitaccounting)|false|none|If true, the amounts of debits on the reports are quoted positive with the related consequence for balances.<br>If false, the amount of debits on the reports are quoted negative.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_challengeData">challengeData</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
{
  "additionalInformation": "string",
  "data": [
    "string"
  ],
  "image": "string",
  "imageLink": "string",
  "otpFormat": "characters",
  "otpMaxLength": 0
}
```

It is contained in addition to the data element 'chosenScaMethod' if challenge data is needed for SCA.
In rare cases this attribute is also used in the context of the 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication' link.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|additionalInformation|string|false|none|Additional explanation for the PSU to explain<br>e.g. fallback mechanism for the chosen SCA method.<br>The TPP is obliged to show this to the PSU.<br>|
|data|[string]|false|none|A collection of strings as challenge data.|
|image|string(byte)|false|none|PNG data (max. 512 kilobyte) to be displayed to the PSU,<br>Base64 encoding, cp. [RFC4648].<br>This attribute is used only, when PHOTO_OTP or CHIP_OTP<br>is the selected SCA method.<br>|
|imageLink|string|false|none|A link where the ASPSP will provides the challenge image for the TPP.|
|otpFormat|string|false|none|The format type of the OTP to be typed in. The admitted values are "characters" or "integer".|
|otpMaxLength|integer|false|none|The maximal length for the OTP to be typed in by the PSU.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|otpFormat|characters|
|otpFormat|integer|

<h2 id="tocS_chosenScaMethod">chosenScaMethod</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemachosenscamethod"></a>
<a id="schema_chosenScaMethod"></a>
<a id="tocSchosenscamethod"></a>
<a id="tocschosenscamethod"></a>

```json
{
  "authenticationMethodId": "myAuthenticationID",
  "authenticationType": "SMS_OTP",
  "authenticationVersion": "string",
  "explanation": "Detailed information about the SCA method for the PSU.",
  "name": "SMS OTP on phone +49160 xxxxx 28"
}
```

Authentication object.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authenticationMethodId|[authenticationMethodId](#schemaauthenticationmethodid)|true|none|An identification provided by the ASPSP for the later identification of the authentication method selection.<br>|
|authenticationType|[authenticationType](#schemaauthenticationtype)|true|none|Type of the authentication method.<br><br>More authentication types might be added during implementation projects and documented in the ASPSP documentation.<br><br>  - 'SMS_OTP': An SCA method, where an OTP linked to the transaction to be authorised is sent to the PSU through a SMS channel.<br>  - 'CHIP_OTP': An SCA method, where an OTP is generated by a chip card, e.g. a TOP derived from an EMV cryptogram. <br>    To contact the card, the PSU normally needs a (handheld) device. <br>    With this device, the PSU either reads the challenging data through a visual interface like flickering or <br>    the PSU types in the challenge through the device key pad. <br>    The device then derives an OTP from the challenge data and displays the OTP to the PSU.<br>  - 'PHOTO_OTP': An SCA method, where the challenge is a QR code or similar encoded visual data<br>    which can be read in by a consumer device or specific mobile app.<br>    The device resp. the specific app than derives an OTP from the visual challenge data and displays<br>    the OTP to the PSU.<br>  - 'PUSH_OTP': An OTP is pushed to a dedicated authentication APP and displayed to the PSU.<br>  - 'SMTP_OTP': An OTP is sent via email to the PSU.<br>|
|authenticationVersion|string|false|none|Depending on the "authenticationType".<br>This version can be used by differentiating authentication tools used within performing OTP generation in the same authentication type.<br>This version can be referred to in the ASPSP?s documentation.<br>|
|explanation|string|false|none|Detailed information about the SCA method for the PSU.<br>|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the authentication method defined by the PSU in the Online Banking frontend of the ASPSP.<br>Alternatively this could be a description provided by the ASPSP like "SMS OTP on phone +49160 xxxxx 28".<br>This name shall be used by the TPP when presenting a list of authentication methods to the PSU, if available.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|authenticationType|SMS_OTP|
|authenticationType|CHIP_OTP|
|authenticationType|PHOTO_OTP|
|authenticationType|PUSH_OTP|
|authenticationType|SMTP_OTP|

<h2 id="tocS_consentStatus">consentStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaconsentstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_consentStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSconsentstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsconsentstatus"></a>

```json
"received"
```

This is the overall lifecycle status of the consent.

Valid values are:
  - 'received': The consent data have been received and are technically correct.
    The data is not authorised yet.
  - 'rejected': The consent data have been rejected e.g. since no successful authorisation has taken place.
  - 'valid': The consent is accepted and valid for GET account data calls and others as specified in the consent object.
  - 'revokedByPsu': The consent has been revoked by the PSU towards the ASPSP.
  - 'expired': The consent expired.
  - 'terminatedByTpp': The corresponding TPP has terminated the consent by applying the DELETE method to the consent resource.
  - 'partiallyAuthorised': The consent is due to a multi-level authorisation, some but not all mandated authorisations have been performed yet.

The ASPSP might add further codes. These codes then shall be contained in the ASPSP's documentation of the XS2A interface 
and has to be added to this API definition as well.

These codes then shall be contained in the ASPSP's documentation of the XS2A interface <br>and has to be added to this API definition as well.<br>|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksConsents](#schema_linksconsents)|true|none|A list of hyperlinks to be recognised by the TPP.<br><br>Type of links admitted in this response (which might be extended by single ASPSPs as indicated in its XS2A<br>documentation):<br>  * 'scaRedirect': <br>    In case of an SCA Redirect Approach, the ASPSP is transmitting the link to which to redirect the <br>    PSU browser.<br>  * 'scaOAuth': <br>    In case of an OAuth2 based Redirect Approach, the ASPSP is transmitting the link where the configuration <br>    of the OAuth2 Server is defined. <br>    The configuration follows the OAuth 2.0 Authorisation Server Metadata specification. <br>* 'confirmation': <br>  Might be added by the ASPSP if either the "scaRedirect" or "scaOAuth" hyperlink is returned <br>  in the same response message. <br>  This hyperlink defines the URL to the resource which needs to be updated with <br>    * a confirmation code as retrieved after the plain redirect authentication process with the ASPSP authentication server or<br>    * an access token as retrieved by submitting an authorization code after the integrated OAuth based authentication process with the ASPSP authentication server.<br>  * 'startAuthorisation': <br>    In case, where an explicit start of the transaction authorisation is needed, <br>    but no more data needs to be updated (no authentication method to be selected, <br>    no PSU identification nor PSU authentication data to be uploaded).<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithPsuIdentification': <br>    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated <br>    while uploading the PSU identification data.<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication':<br>    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated <br>    while uploading the PSU authentication data.<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithEncryptedPsuAuthentication':<br>    Same as startAuthorisactionWithPsuAuthentication where the authentication data need to be encrypted on<br>    application layer in uploading.<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection':<br>    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated <br>    while selecting the authentication method. This link is contained under exactly the same conditions <br>    as the data element 'scaMethods' <br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithTransactionAuthorisation':<br>    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated <br>    while authorising the transaction e.g. by uploading an OTP received by SMS.<br>  * 'self': <br>    The link to the Establish Account Information Consent resource created by this request. <br>    This link can be used to retrieve the resource data. <br>  * 'status': <br>    The link to retrieve the status of the account information consent.<br>  * 'scaStatus': The link to retrieve the scaStatus of the corresponding authorisation sub-resource. <br>    This link is only contained, if an authorisation sub-resource has been already created.<br>|
|challengeData|[challengeData](#schemachallengedata)|false|none|It is contained in addition to the data element 'chosenScaMethod' if challenge data is needed for SCA.<br>In rare cases this attribute is also used in the context of the 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication' link.<br>|
|chosenScaMethod|[authenticationObject](#schemaauthenticationobject)|false|none|Authentication object.<br>|
|consentId|[consentId](#schemaconsentid)|true|none|ID of the corresponding consent object as returned by an account information consent request.<br>|
|consentStatus|[consentStatus](#schemaconsentstatus)|true|none|This is the overall lifecycle status of the consent.<br><br>Valid values are:<br>  - 'received': The consent data have been received and are technically correct.<br>    The data is not authorised yet.<br>  - 'rejected': The consent data have been rejected e.g. since no successful authorisation has taken place.<br>  - 'valid': The consent is accepted and valid for GET account data calls and others as specified in the consent object.<br>  - 'revokedByPsu': The consent has been revoked by the PSU towards the ASPSP.<br>  - 'expired': The consent expired.<br>  - 'terminatedByTpp': The corresponding TPP has terminated the consent by applying the DELETE method to the consent resource.<br>  - 'partiallyAuthorised': The consent is due to a multi-level authorisation, some but not all mandated authorisations have been performed yet.<br><br>The ASPSP might add further codes. These codes then shall be contained in the ASPSP's documentation of the XS2A interface <br>and has to be added to this API definition as well.<br>|
|psuMessage|[psuMessageText](#schemapsumessagetext)|false|none|Text to be displayed to the PSU.|
|scaMethods|[scaMethods](#schemascamethods)|false|none|This data element might be contained, if SCA is required and if the PSU has a choice between different<br>authentication methods.<br><br>Depending on the risk management of the ASPSP this choice might be offered before or after the PSU<br>has been identified with the first relevant factor, or if an access token is transported.<br><br>If this data element is contained, then there is also a hyperlink of type 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection'<br>contained in the response body.<br><br>These methods shall be presented towards the PSU for selection by the TPP.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|consentStatus|received|
|consentStatus|rejected|
|consentStatus|valid|
|consentStatus|revokedByPsu|
|consentStatus|expired|
|consentStatus|terminatedByTpp|
|consentStatus|partiallyAuthorised|

The array is restricted to 11 entries. 
The values contained in the array entries shall all be different and the maximum value of one entry is 12.

Body of the response for a successful payment initiation request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksPaymentInitiation](#schema_linkspaymentinitiation)|true|none|A list of hyperlinks to be recognised by the TPP.<br>The actual hyperlinks used in the response depend on the dynamical decisions of the ASPSP when<br>processing the request.<br><br>**Remark:** All links can be relative or full links, to be decided by the ASPSP.<br><br>Type of links admitted in this response, (further links might be added for ASPSP defined extensions):<br><br>* 'scaRedirect':<br>  In case of an SCA Redirect Approach, the ASPSP is transmitting the link to which to redirect the PSU browser.<br>* 'scaOAuth':<br>  In case of a SCA OAuth2 Approach, the ASPSP is transmitting the URI where the configuration of the Authorisation<br>  Server can be retrieved. The configuration follows the OAuth 2.0 Authorisation Server Metadata specification.<br>* 'confirmation': <br>  Might be added by the ASPSP if either the "scaRedirect" or "scaOAuth" hyperlink is returned <br>  in the same response message. <br>  This hyperlink defines the URL to the resource which needs to be updated with <br>    * a confirmation code as retrieved after the plain redirect authentication process with the ASPSP authentication server or<br>    * an access token as retrieved by submitting an authorization code after the integrated OAuth based authentication process with the ASPSP authentication server. <br>* 'startAuthorisation': <br>  In case, where an explicit start of the transaction authorisation is needed, but no more data needs to be updated <br>  (no authentication method to be selected, no PSU identification nor PSU authentication data to be uploaded).<br>* 'startAuthorisationWithPsuIdentification':<br>  The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated while<br>  uploading the PSU identification data.<br>* 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication':<br>  The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated while<br>  uploading the PSU authentication data.<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithEncryptedPsuAuthentication':<br>    Same as startAuthorisactionWithPsuAuthentication where the authentication data need to be encrypted on<br>    application layer in uploading.<br>* 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection':<br>  The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated while<br>  selecting the authentication method.<br>  This link is contained under exactly the same conditions as the data element "scaMethods"<br>* 'startAuthorisationWithTransactionAuthorisation':<br>  The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated while<br>  authorising the transaction e.g. by uploading an OTP received by SMS.<br>* 'self':<br>  The link to the payment initiation resource created by this request.<br>  This link can be used to retrieve the resource data.<br>* 'status':<br>  The link to retrieve the transaction status of the payment initiation.<br>* 'scaStatus':<br>  The link to retrieve the scaStatus of the corresponding authorisation sub-resource.<br>  This link is only contained, if an authorisation sub-resource has been already created.<br>|
|challengeData|[challengeData](#schemachallengedata)|false|none|It is contained in addition to the data element 'chosenScaMethod' if challenge data is needed for SCA.<br>In rare cases this attribute is also used in the context of the 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication' link.<br>|
|chosenScaMethod|[authenticationObject](#schemaauthenticationobject)|false|none|Authentication object.<br>|
|currencyConversionFee|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|none|
|estimatedInterbankSettlementAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|none|
|estimatedTotalAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|none|
|paymentId|[paymentId](#schemapaymentid)|true|none|Resource identification of the generated payment initiation resource.|
|psuMessage|[psuMessageText](#schemapsumessagetext)|false|none|Text to be displayed to the PSU.|
|scaMethods|[scaMethods](#schemascamethods)|false|none|This data element might be contained, if SCA is required and if the PSU has a choice between different<br>authentication methods.<br><br>Depending on the risk management of the ASPSP this choice might be offered before or after the PSU<br>has been identified with the first relevant factor, or if an access token is transported.<br><br>If this data element is contained, then there is also a hyperlink of type 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection'<br>contained in the response body.<br><br>These methods shall be presented towards the PSU for selection by the TPP.<br>|
|tppMessages|[[tppMessage2XX](#schematppmessage2xx)]|false|none|none|
|transactionFeeIndicator|[transactionFeeIndicator](#schematransactionfeeindicator)|false|none|If equals 'true', the transaction will involve specific transaction cost as shown by the ASPSP in<br>their public price list or as agreed between ASPSP and PSU.<br>If equals 'false', the transaction will not involve additional specific transaction costs to the PSU unless the fee amount is given specifically in the data elements transactionFees and/or currencyConversionFees.<br>If this data element is not used, there is no information about transaction fees unless the fee amount is given explicitly in the data element transactionFees and/or currencyConversionFees.<br>|
|transactionFees|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|none|
|transactionStatus|[transactionStatus](#schematransactionstatus)|true|none|The transaction status is filled with codes of the ISO 20022 data table:<br>- 'ACCC': 'AcceptedSettlementCompleted' -<br>  Settlement on the creditor's account has been completed.<br>- 'ACCP': 'AcceptedCustomerProfile' -<br>  Preceding check of technical validation was successful.<br>  Customer profile check was also successful.<br>- 'ACSC': 'AcceptedSettlementCompleted' -<br>  Settlement on the debtoro?=s account has been completed.<br><br>  **Usage:** this can be used by the first agent to report to the debtor that the transaction has been completed.<br><br>  **Warning:** this status is provided for transaction status reasons, not for financial information.<br>  It can only be used after bilateral agreement.<br>- 'ACSP': 'AcceptedSettlementInProcess' -<br>  All preceding checks such as technical validation and customer profile were successful and therefore the payment initiation has been accepted for execution.<br>- 'ACTC': 'AcceptedTechnicalValidation' -<br>  Authentication and syntactical and semantical validation are successful.<br>- 'ACWC': 'AcceptedWithChange' -<br>  Instruction is accepted but a change will be made, such as date or remittance not sent.<br>- 'ACWP': 'AcceptedWithoutPosting' -<br>  Payment instruction included in the credit transfer is accepted without being posted to the creditor customero?=s account.<br>- 'RCVD': 'Received' -<br>  Payment initiation has been received by the receiving agent.<br>- 'PDNG': 'Pending' -<br>  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation is pending.<br>  Further checks and status update will be performed.<br>- 'RJCT': 'Rejected' -<br>  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation has been rejected.<br>- 'CANC': 'Cancelled'<br>  Payment initiation has been cancelled before execution<br>  Remark: This codeis accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'ACFC': 'AcceptedFundsChecked' -<br>  Preceding check of technical validation and customer profile was successful and an automatic funds check was positive .<br>  Remark: This code is accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'PATC': 'PartiallyAcceptedTechnical'<br>  Correct The payment initiation needs multiple authentications, where some but not yet all have been performed. Syntactical and semantical validations are successful.<br>  Remark: This code is accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'PART': 'PartiallyAccepted' -<br>  A number of transactions have been accepted, whereas another number of transactions have not yet achieved 'accepted' status.<br>  Remark: This code may be used only in case of bulk payments. It is only used in a situation where all mandated authorisations have been applied, but some payments have been rejected.<br>|

Generic body for a bulk payment initation entry.

The bulk entry type is a type which follows the JSON formats for the supported products for single payments
excluding the data elements (if supported):
  * debtorAccount
  * requestedExecutionDate,
  * requestedExecutionTime.
These data elements may not be contained in any bulk entry.

This data object can be used to represent valid bulk payment initiations entry for the following JSON based payment product,
which where defined in the Implementation Guidelines:

  * domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-isr
  * domestic-swiss-credit-transfers
  * domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-qr
  * domestic-swiss-foreign-credit-transfers
  * swiss-sepa-credit-transfers
  * swiss-cross-border-credit-transfers

For the convenience of the implementer additional which are already predefinded in the Implementation Guidelines
are included (but commented in source code), such that an ASPSP may add them easily.

Take care: Since the format is intended to fit for all payment products
there are additional conditions which are NOT covered by this specification.
Please check the SIX Swiss Payment Standards implementation guidelines for details.

Footnotes from the table:
1) This element may only be used by agreement with the instructed financial institution.
2) The element may only be used in consultation with the financial institution commissioned.
3) The element is currently ignored by financial institutions.
4) Dependence on creditorAccount, see SIX Swiss Payments Standards implementation guidelines.
5) Type 4(V3), 6(V2, V3): Must be present. Type 4(V2): May be present. Other species: May not be present.
6) QR-reference, creditor reference or IPI reference
7) currencyOfTransfer is a subfield of equivalentAmount and may only be used if equivalentAmount is used instead of instructedAmount.
8) QR-IBAN (CH/LI) must be present.

IMPORTANT: In this API definition the following holds:
  *  All data elements mentioned above are defined, but some of them are commented,
    i.e. they are only visible in the source code and can be used by uncommenting them.
  * Data elements which are mandatory in the table above for all payment products
    are set to be mandatory in this specification.
  * Data elements which are indicated in the table above as n.a. for all payment products are commented in the source code.
  * Data elements which are indicated to be option, conditional or mandatory for at least one payment product
    in the table above are set to be optional in the s specification except the case where all are definde to be mandatory.
  * Data element which are inticated to be n.a. can be used by the ASPS if needed.
    In this case uncomment tthe the relatetd lines in the source code.
  * If one uses this data types for some payment products he has to ensure that the used data type is
    valid according to the underlying payment product, e.g. by some appropriate validations.

Body of the response for a successful cancel payment request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksPaymentInitiationCancel](#schema_linkspaymentinitiationcancel)|false|none|A list of hyperlinks to be recognised by the TPP. The actual hyperlinks used in the response depend on the<br>dynamical decisions of the ASPSP when processing the request.<br><br>Remark: All links can be relative or full links, to be decided by the ASPSP.<br><br>Type of links admitted in this response, (further links might be added for ASPSP defined extensions):<br><br>  * 'startAuthorisation':<br>    In case, where just the authorisation process of the cancellation needs to be started,<br>    but no additional data needs to be updated for time being (no authentication method to be selected,<br>    no PSU identification nor PSU authentication data to be uploaded).<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithPsuIdentification': <br>    In case where a PSU identification needs to be updated when starting the cancellation authorisation:<br>    The link to the cancellation-authorisations end-point, where the cancellation sub-resource has to be <br>    generated while uploading the PSU identification data.<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication':<br>    In case of a yet to be created authorisation sub-resource: The link to the cancalation authorisation end-point,<br>    where the authorisation sub-resource has to be generated while uploading the PSU authentication data.<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithEncryptedPsuAuthentication':<br>    Same as startAuthorisactionWithPsuAuthentication where the authentication data need to be encrypted on<br>    application layer in uploading.<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection':<br>    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the cancellation-authorisation sub-resource has to be<br>    generated while selecting the authentication method. This link is contained under exactly the same<br>    conditions as the data element 'scaMethods'<br>|
|challengeData|[challengeData](#schemachallengedata)|false|none|It is contained in addition to the data element 'chosenScaMethod' if challenge data is needed for SCA.<br>In rare cases this attribute is also used in the context of the 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication' link.<br>|
|chosenScaMethod|[authenticationObject](#schemaauthenticationobject)|false|none|Authentication object.<br>|
|scaMethods|[scaMethods](#schemascamethods)|false|none|This data element might be contained, if SCA is required and if the PSU has a choice between different<br>authentication methods.<br><br>Depending on the risk management of the ASPSP this choice might be offered before or after the PSU<br>has been identified with the first relevant factor, or if an access token is transported.<br><br>If this data element is contained, then there is also a hyperlink of type 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection'<br>contained in the response body.<br><br>These methods shall be presented towards the PSU for selection by the TPP.<br>|
|transactionStatus|[transactionStatus](#schematransactionstatus)|true|none|The transaction status is filled with codes of the ISO 20022 data table:<br>- 'ACCC': 'AcceptedSettlementCompleted' -<br>  Settlement on the creditor's account has been completed.<br>- 'ACCP': 'AcceptedCustomerProfile' -<br>  Preceding check of technical validation was successful.<br>  Customer profile check was also successful.<br>- 'ACSC': 'AcceptedSettlementCompleted' -<br>  Settlement on the debtoro?=s account has been completed.<br><br>  **Usage:** this can be used by the first agent to report to the debtor that the transaction has been completed.<br><br>  **Warning:** this status is provided for transaction status reasons, not for financial information.<br>  It can only be used after bilateral agreement.<br>- 'ACSP': 'AcceptedSettlementInProcess' -<br>  All preceding checks such as technical validation and customer profile were successful and therefore the payment initiation has been accepted for execution.<br>- 'ACTC': 'AcceptedTechnicalValidation' -<br>  Authentication and syntactical and semantical validation are successful.<br>- 'ACWC': 'AcceptedWithChange' -<br>  Instruction is accepted but a change will be made, such as date or remittance not sent.<br>- 'ACWP': 'AcceptedWithoutPosting' -<br>  Payment instruction included in the credit transfer is accepted without being posted to the creditor customero?=s account.<br>- 'RCVD': 'Received' -<br>  Payment initiation has been received by the receiving agent.<br>- 'PDNG': 'Pending' -<br>  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation is pending.<br>  Further checks and status update will be performed.<br>- 'RJCT': 'Rejected' -<br>  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation has been rejected.<br>- 'CANC': 'Cancelled'<br>  Payment initiation has been cancelled before execution<br>  Remark: This codeis accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'ACFC': 'AcceptedFundsChecked' -<br>  Preceding check of technical validation and customer profile was successful and an automatic funds check was positive .<br>  Remark: This code is accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'PATC': 'PartiallyAcceptedTechnical'<br>  Correct The payment initiation needs multiple authentications, where some but not yet all have been performed. Syntactical and semantical validations are successful.<br>  Remark: This code is accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'PART': 'PartiallyAccepted' -<br>  A number of transactions have been accepted, whereas another number of transactions have not yet achieved 'accepted' status.<br>  Remark: This code may be used only in case of bulk payments. It is only used in a situation where all mandated authorisations have been applied, but some payments have been rejected.<br>|

|transactionStatus|RCVD|
|transactionStatus|PDNG|
|transactionStatus|RJCT|
|transactionStatus|CANC|
|transactionStatus|ACFC|
|transactionStatus|PATC|
|transactionStatus|PART|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fundsAvailable|[fundsAvailable](#schemafundsavailable)|false|none|Equals true if sufficient funds are available at the time of the request, false otherwise.<br><br>This datalemenet is allways contained in a confirmation of funds response.<br><br>This data element is contained in a payment status response, <br>if supported by the ASPSP, if a funds check has been performed and <br>if the transactionStatus is "ACTC", "ACWC" or "ACCP".<br>|
|psuMessage|[psuMessageText](#schemapsumessagetext)|false|none|Text to be displayed to the PSU.|
|transactionStatus|[transactionStatus](#schematransactionstatus)|true|none|The transaction status is filled with codes of the ISO 20022 data table:<br>- 'ACCC': 'AcceptedSettlementCompleted' -<br>  Settlement on the creditor's account has been completed.<br>- 'ACCP': 'AcceptedCustomerProfile' -<br>  Preceding check of technical validation was successful.<br>  Customer profile check was also successful.<br>- 'ACSC': 'AcceptedSettlementCompleted' -<br>  Settlement on the debtoro?=s account has been completed.<br><br>  **Usage:** this can be used by the first agent to report to the debtor that the transaction has been completed.<br><br>  **Warning:** this status is provided for transaction status reasons, not for financial information.<br>  It can only be used after bilateral agreement.<br>- 'ACSP': 'AcceptedSettlementInProcess' -<br>  All preceding checks such as technical validation and customer profile were successful and therefore the payment initiation has been accepted for execution.<br>- 'ACTC': 'AcceptedTechnicalValidation' -<br>  Authentication and syntactical and semantical validation are successful.<br>- 'ACWC': 'AcceptedWithChange' -<br>  Instruction is accepted but a change will be made, such as date or remittance not sent.<br>- 'ACWP': 'AcceptedWithoutPosting' -<br>  Payment instruction included in the credit transfer is accepted without being posted to the creditor customero?=s account.<br>- 'RCVD': 'Received' -<br>  Payment initiation has been received by the receiving agent.<br>- 'PDNG': 'Pending' -<br>  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation is pending.<br>  Further checks and status update will be performed.<br>- 'RJCT': 'Rejected' -<br>  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation has been rejected.<br>- 'CANC': 'Cancelled'<br>  Payment initiation has been cancelled before execution<br>  Remark: This codeis accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'ACFC': 'AcceptedFundsChecked' -<br>  Preceding check of technical validation and customer profile was successful and an automatic funds check was positive .<br>  Remark: This code is accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'PATC': 'PartiallyAcceptedTechnical'<br>  Correct The payment initiation needs multiple authentications, where some but not yet all have been performed. Syntactical and semantical validations are successful.<br>  Remark: This code is accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'PART': 'PartiallyAccepted' -<br>  A number of transactions have been accepted, whereas another number of transactions have not yet achieved 'accepted' status.<br>  Remark: This code may be used only in case of bulk payments. It is only used in a situation where all mandated authorisations have been applied, but some payments have been rejected.<br>|

|transactionStatus|RCVD|
|transactionStatus|PDNG|
|transactionStatus|RJCT|
|transactionStatus|CANC|
|transactionStatus|ACFC|
|transactionStatus|PATC|
|transactionStatus|PART|

Generic Body for a payment initation via JSON.

This generic JSON body can be used to represent valid payment initiations for the following JSON based payment product,
which where defined in the Implementation Guidelines:

  * domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-isr
  * domestic-swiss-credit-transfers
  * domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-qr
  * domestic-swiss-foreign-credit-transfers
  * swiss-sepa-credit-transfers
  * swiss-cross-border-credit-transfers

For the convenience of the implementer additional which are already predefinded in the Implementation Guidelines
are included (but commented in source code), such that an ASPSP may add them easily.

Take care: Since the format is intended to fit for all payment products
there are additional conditions which are NOT covered by this specification.
Please check the SIX Swiss Payment Standards implementation guidelines for details.

Footnotes from the table:
1) This element may only be used by agreement with the instructed financial institution.
2) The element may only be used in consultation with the financial institution commissioned.
3) The element is currently ignored by financial institutions.
4) Dependence on creditorAccount, see SIX Swiss Payments Standards implementation guidelines.
5) Type 4(V3), 6(V2, V3): Must be present. Type 4(V2): May be present. Other species: May not be present.
6) QR-reference, creditor reference or IPI reference
7) transactionCurrency is a subfield of equivalentAmount and may only be used if equivalentAmount is used instead of instructedAmount.
8) QR-IBAN (CH/LI) must be present.

IMPORTANT: In this API definition the following holds:
  *  All data elements mentioned above are defined, but some of them are commented,
    i.e. they are only visible in the source code and can be used by uncommenting them.
  * Data elements which are mandatory in the table above for all payment products
    are set to be mandatory in this specification.
  * Data elements which are indicated in the table above as n.a. for all payment products are commented in the source code.
  * Data elements which are indicated to be option, conditional or mandatory for at least one payment product
    in the table above are set to be optional in the s specification except the case where all are definde to be mandatory.
  * Data element which are inticated to be n.a. can be used by the ASPS if needed.
    In this case uncomment tthe the relatetd lines in the source code.
  * If one uses this data types for some payment products he has to ensure that the used data type is
    valid according to the underlying payment product, e.g. by some appropriate validations.
