where the information of the payment is contained in a pain.001 message (Part 1) and 
the additional informations related to the periodic payment is an additional JSON message (Part 2).

Generic JSON response body consistion of the corresponding periodic payment initation JSON body together with an optional transaction status field.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|creditorAccount|[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)|true|none|Reference to an account by either<br>  * IBAN, of a payment accounts, or<br>  * otherAccountIdentification, for payment accounts if there is no IBAN<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 CashAccount16-CH_IdTpCcy<br>|
|creditorAddress|[address](#schemaaddress)|false|none|none|
|creditorAgent|[creditorAgent7-CH](#schemacreditoragent7-ch)|false|none|Reference to an creditorAgent by either<br>  * BIC, of the creditor bank, or<br>  * IID, of the creditor bank, or<br>  * IID and optional name and address of the creditor bank or<br>  * Name and address of the creditor bank<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 FinancialInstitutionIdentification7-CH<br>|
|creditorName|[creditorName](#schemacreditorname)|true|none|Creditor name.|
|dayOfExecution|[dayOfExecution](#schemadayofexecution)|false|none|Day of execution as string.<br><br>This string consists of up two characters.<br>Leading zeroes are not allowed.<br><br>31 is ultimo of the month.<br>|
|debtorAccount|[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)|true|none|Reference to an account by either<br>  * IBAN, of a payment accounts, or<br>  * otherAccountIdentification, for payment accounts if there is no IBAN<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 CashAccount16-CH_IdTpCcy<br>|
|endDate|[endDate](#schemaenddate)|false|none|The last applicable day of execution.<br>If not given, it is an infinite standing order.<br>|
|endToEndIdentification|string|false|none|none|
|executionRule|[executionRule](#schemaexecutionrule)|false|none|"following" or "preceding" supported as values.<br>This data attribute defines the behaviour when recurring payment dates falls on a weekend or bank holiday.<br>The payment is then executed either the "preceding" or "following" working day.<br>ASPSP might reject the request due to the communicated value, if rules in Online-Banking are not supporting<br>this execution rule.<br>|
|frequency|[frequencyCode](#schemafrequencycode)|true|none|The following codes from the "EventFrequency7Code" of ISO 20022 are supported:<br>- "Daily"<br>- "Weekly"<br>- "EveryTwoWeeks"<br>- "Monthly"<br>- "EveryTwoMonths"<br>- "Quarterly"<br>- "SemiAnnual"<br>- "Annual"<br>- "MonthlyVariable"<br>|
|instructedAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|none|
|purposeCode|[purposeCode](#schemapurposecode)|false|none|ExternalPurpose1Code from ISO 20022.<br><br>Values from ISO 20022 External Code List ExternalCodeSets_1Q2018 June 2018.<br>|
|remittanceInformationStructured|[remittanceInformationStructured](#schemaremittanceinformationstructured)|false|none|Structured remittance information.<br>|
|remittanceInformationUnstructured|[remittanceInformationUnstructured](#schemaremittanceinformationunstructured)|false|none|Unstructured remittance information.<br>|
|remittanceInformationUnstructuredArray|[remittanceInformationUnstructuredArray](#schemaremittanceinformationunstructuredarray)|false|none|Array of unstructured remittance information.<br>|
|requestedExecutionDate|string(date)|false|none|none|
|requestedExecutionTime|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|startDate|[startDate](#schemastartdate)|true|none|The first applicable day of execution starting from this date is the first payment.<br>|
|transactionStatus|[transactionStatus](#schematransactionstatus)|false|none|The transaction status is filled with codes of the ISO 20022 data table:<br>- 'ACCC': 'AcceptedSettlementCompleted' -<br>  Settlement on the creditor's account has been completed.<br>- 'ACCP': 'AcceptedCustomerProfile' -<br>  Preceding check of technical validation was successful.<br>  Customer profile check was also successful.<br>- 'ACSC': 'AcceptedSettlementCompleted' -<br>  Settlement on the debtoro?=s account has been completed.<br><br>  **Usage:** this can be used by the first agent to report to the debtor that the transaction has been completed.<br><br>  **Warning:** this status is provided for transaction status reasons, not for financial information.<br>  It can only be used after bilateral agreement.<br>- 'ACSP': 'AcceptedSettlementInProcess' -<br>  All preceding checks such as technical validation and customer profile were successful and therefore the payment initiation has been accepted for execution.<br>- 'ACTC': 'AcceptedTechnicalValidation' -<br>  Authentication and syntactical and semantical validation are successful.<br>- 'ACWC': 'AcceptedWithChange' -<br>  Instruction is accepted but a change will be made, such as date or remittance not sent.<br>- 'ACWP': 'AcceptedWithoutPosting' -<br>  Payment instruction included in the credit transfer is accepted without being posted to the creditor customero?=s account.<br>- 'RCVD': 'Received' -<br>  Payment initiation has been received by the receiving agent.<br>- 'PDNG': 'Pending' -<br>  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation is pending.<br>  Further checks and status update will be performed.<br>- 'RJCT': 'Rejected' -<br>  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation has been rejected.<br>- 'CANC': 'Cancelled'<br>  Payment initiation has been cancelled before execution<br>  Remark: This codeis accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'ACFC': 'AcceptedFundsChecked' -<br>  Preceding check of technical validation and customer profile was successful and an automatic funds check was positive .<br>  Remark: This code is accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'PATC': 'PartiallyAcceptedTechnical'<br>  Correct The payment initiation needs multiple authentications, where some but not yet all have been performed. Syntactical and semantical validations are successful.<br>  Remark: This code is accepted as new code by ISO20022.<br>- 'PART': 'PartiallyAccepted' -<br>  A number of transactions have been accepted, whereas another number of transactions have not yet achieved 'accepted' status.<br>  Remark: This code may be used only in case of bulk payments. It is only used in a situation where all mandated authorisations have been applied, but some payments have been rejected.<br>|
|ultimateCreditor|[ultimateCreditor](#schemaultimatecreditor)|false|none|Ultimate creditor.|
|ultimateDebtor|[ultimateDebtor](#schemaultimatedebtor)|false|none|Ultimate debtor.|

Generic Body for a periodic payment initation via JSON.

This generic JSON body can be used to represent valid periodic payment initiations for the following JSON based payment product,
which where defined in the Implementation Guidelines:

  * domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-isr
  * domestic-swiss-credit-transfers
  * domestic-swiss-credit-transfers-qr
  * domestic-swiss-foreign-credit-transfers
  * swiss-sepa-credit-transfers
  * swiss-cross-border-credit-transfers

For the convenience of the implementer additional which are already predefinded in the Implementation Guidelines
are included (but commented in source code), such that an ASPSP may add them easily.

Take care: Since the format is intended to fit for all payment products
there are additional conditions which are NOT covered by this specification.
Please check the SIX Swiss Payment Standards implementation guidelines for details.


The following data element are depending on the actual payment product available (in source code):

Footnotes from the table:
1) This element may only be used by agreement with the instructed financial institution.
2) The element may only be used in consultation with the financial institution commissioned.
3) The element is currently ignored by financial institutions.
4) Dependence on creditorAccount, see SIX Swiss Payments Standards implementation guidelines.
5) Type 4(V3), 6(V2, V3): Must be present. Type 4(V2): May be present. Other species: May not be present.
6) QR-reference, creditor reference or IPI reference
7) currencyOfTransfer is a subfield of equivalentAmount and may only be used if equivalentAmount is used instead of instructedAmount.
8) QR-IBAN (CH/LI) must be present.

IMPORTANT: In this API definition the following holds:
  *  All data elements mentioned above are defined, but some of them are commented,
    i.e. they are only visible in the source code and can be used by uncommenting them.
  * Data elements which are mandatory in the table above for all payment products
    are set to be mandatory in this specification.
  * Data elements which are indicated in the table above as n.a. for all payment products are commented in the source code.
  * Data elements which are indicated to be option, conditional or mandatory for at least one payment product
    in the table above are set to be optional in the s specification except the case where all are definde to be mandatory.
  * Data element which are inticated to be n.a. can be used by the ASPS if needed.
    In this case uncomment tthe the relatetd lines in the source code.
  * If one uses this data types for some payment products he has to ensure that the used data type is
    valid according to the underlying payment product, e.g. by some appropriate validations.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|chargeBearer|[chargeBearer](#schemachargebearer)|false|none|Charge Bearer. ChargeBearerType1Code from ISO20022.|
|creditorAccount|[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)|true|none|Reference to an account by either<br>  * IBAN, of a payment accounts, or<br>  * otherAccountIdentification, for payment accounts if there is no IBAN<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 CashAccount16-CH_IdTpCcy<br>|
|creditorAddress|[address](#schemaaddress)|false|none|none|
|creditorAgent|[creditorAgent7-CH](#schemacreditoragent7-ch)|false|none|Reference to an creditorAgent by either<br>  * BIC, of the creditor bank, or<br>  * IID, of the creditor bank, or<br>  * IID and optional name and address of the creditor bank or<br>  * Name and address of the creditor bank<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 FinancialInstitutionIdentification7-CH<br>|
|creditorAgentName|[creditorAgentName](#schemacreditoragentname)|false|none|Creditor agent name.|

|debtorAccount|[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)|true|none|Reference to an account by either<br>  * IBAN, of a payment accounts, or<br>  * otherAccountIdentification, for payment accounts if there is no IBAN<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 CashAccount16-CH_IdTpCcy<br>|
|debtorAgent|[debtorAgent7-CH](#schemadebtoragent7-ch)|false|none|Reference to an debtorAgent by either<br>  * BIC, of the debtor bank, or<br>  * IID, of the debtor bank<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 FinancialInstitutionIdentification7-CH_BicOrClrId<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_scaMethods">scaMethods</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemascamethods"></a>
<a id="schema_scaMethods"></a>
<a id="tocSscamethods"></a>
<a id="tocsscamethods"></a>

```json
[
  {
    "authenticationMethodId": "myAuthenticationID",
    "authenticationType": "SMS_OTP",
    "authenticationVersion": "string",
    "explanation": "Detailed information about the SCA method for the PSU.",
    "name": "SMS OTP on phone +49160 xxxxx 28"
  }
]
```

This data element might be contained, if SCA is required and if the PSU has a choice between different
authentication methods.

Depending on the risk management of the ASPSP this choice might be offered before or after the PSU
has been identified with the first relevant factor, or if an access token is transported.

If this data element is contained, then there is also a hyperlink of type 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection'
contained in the response body.

These methods shall be presented towards the PSU for selection by the TPP.

<h2 id="tocS_scaStatus">scaStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemascastatus"></a>
<a id="schema_scaStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSscastatus"></a>
<a id="tocsscastatus"></a>

```json
"psuAuthenticated"
```

This data element is containing information about the status of the SCA method applied.

The following codes are defined for this data type.

  * 'received':
    An authorisation or cancellation-authorisation resource has been created successfully.
  * 'psuIdentified':
    The PSU related to the authorisation or cancellation-authorisation resource has been identified.
  * 'psuAuthenticated':
    The PSU related to the authorisation or cancellation-authorisation resource has been identified and authenticated e.g. by a password or by an access token.
  * 'scaMethodSelected':
    The PSU/TPP has selected the related SCA routine.
    If the SCA method is chosen implicitly since only one SCA method is available,
    then this is the first status to be reported instead of 'received'.
  * 'unconfirmed':
    SCA is technically successfully finalised by the PSU, but the authorisation resource needs a confirmation command by the TPP yet. 
  * 'started':
    The addressed SCA routine has been started.
  * 'finalised':
    The SCA routine has been finalised successfully (including a potential confirmation command). 
    This is a final status of the authorisation resource.
  * 'failed':
    The SCA routine failed.
    This is a final status of the authorisation resource.
  * 'exempted':
    SCA was exempted for the related transaction, the related authorisation is successful.
    This is a final status of the authorisation resource.

<h2 id="tocS_scaStatusAuthorisationConfirmation">scaStatusAuthorisationConfirmation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemascastatusauthorisationconfirmation"></a>
<a id="schema_scaStatusAuthorisationConfirmation"></a>
<a id="tocSscastatusauthorisationconfirmation"></a>
<a id="tocsscastatusauthorisationconfirmation"></a>

```json
"finalised"
```

This data element is containing information about the status of the SCA method in an authorisation confirmation response. 

The following codes are defined for this data type.

  * 'finalised': if the transaction authorisation and confirmation was successfule.
  * 'failed': if the transaction authorisation or confirmation was not successful.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|psuMessage|[psuMessageText](#schemapsumessagetext)|false|none|Text to be displayed to the PSU.|
|scaStatus|[scaStatus](#schemascastatus)|true|none|This data element is containing information about the status of the SCA method applied.<br><br>The following codes are defined for this data type.<br><br>  * 'received':<br>    An authorisation or cancellation-authorisation resource has been created successfully.<br>  * 'psuIdentified':<br>    The PSU related to the authorisation or cancellation-authorisation resource has been identified.<br>  * 'psuAuthenticated':<br>    The PSU related to the authorisation or cancellation-authorisation resource has been identified and authenticated e.g. by a password or by an access token.<br>  * 'scaMethodSelected':<br>    The PSU/TPP has selected the related SCA routine.<br>    If the SCA method is chosen implicitly since only one SCA method is available,<br>    then this is the first status to be reported instead of 'received'.<br>  * 'unconfirmed':<br>    SCA is technically successfully finalised by the PSU, but the authorisation resource needs a confirmation command by the TPP yet. <br>  * 'started':<br>    The addressed SCA routine has been started.<br>  * 'finalised':<br>    The SCA routine has been finalised successfully (including a potential confirmation command). <br>    This is a final status of the authorisation resource.<br>  * 'failed':<br>    The SCA routine failed.<br>    This is a final status of the authorisation resource.<br>  * 'exempted':<br>    SCA was exempted for the related transaction, the related authorisation is successful.<br>    This is a final status of the authorisation resource.<br>|
|trustedBeneficiaryFlag|[trustedBeneficiaryFlag](#schematrustedbeneficiaryflag)|false|none|Additional Service: Trusted Benificiaries<br>Within this data element, the ASPSP might optionally communicate towards the TPP whether the creditor was part of the related trusted beneficiary list. <br>This attribute is only contained in case of a final scaStatus.<br>|

|scaStatus|psuIdentified|
|scaStatus|psuAuthenticated|
|scaStatus|scaMethodSelected|
|scaStatus|started|
|scaStatus|unconfirmed|
|scaStatus|finalised|
|scaStatus|failed|
|scaStatus|exempted|

'updateEncryptedPsuAuthentication':<br>  The link to the authorisation or cancellation authorisation sub-resource,<br>  where PSU authentication encrypted data needs to be uploaded.<br>- 'updateAdditionalPsuAuthentication':<br>    The link to the payment initiation or account information resource,<br>    which needs to be updated by an additional PSU password.<br>- 'updateAdditionalEncryptedPsuAuthentication':<br>    The link to the payment initiation or account information resource,<br>    which needs to be updated by an additional encrypted PSU password.<br>- 'authoriseTransaction':<br>  The link to the authorisation or cancellation authorisation sub-resource,<br>  where the authorisation data has to be uploaded, e.g. the TOP received by SMS.<br>- 'scaStatus':<br>  The link to retrieve the scaStatus of the corresponding authorisation sub-resource.<br>|

Body of the JSON response for a successful get signing basket request.

  * 'payments': payment initiations which shall be authorised through this signing basket.
  * 'consents': consent objects which shall be authorised through this signing basket.
  * 'transactionStatus': Only the codes RCVD, ACTC, RJCT are used.
  * '_links': The ASPSP might integrate hyperlinks to indicate next (authorisation) steps to be taken.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksSigningBasket](#schema_linkssigningbasket)|false|none|A list of hyperlinks to be recognised by the TPP. The actual hyperlinks used in the<br>response depend on the dynamical decisions of the ASPSP when processing the request.<br><br>Remark: All links can be relative or full links, to be decided by the ASPSP.<br>Type of links admitted in this response, (further links might be added for ASPSP defined<br>extensions):<br><br>  * 'scaRedirect':<br>    In case of an SCA Redirect Approach, the ASPSP is transmitting the link to<br>    which to redirect the PSU browser.<br>  * 'scaOAuth':<br>    In case of a SCA OAuth2 Approach, the ASPSP is transmitting the URI where the configuration of<br>    the Authorisation Server can be retrieved. The configuration follows the<br>    OAuth 2.0 Authorisation Server Metadata specification.<br>  * 'startAuthorisation':<br>    In case, where an explicit start of the transaction authorisation is needed,<br>    but no more data needs to be updated (no authentication method to be selected,<br>    no PSU identification nor PSU authentication data to be uploaded).<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithPsuIdentification':<br>    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource<br>    has to be generated while uploading the PSU identification data.<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication':<br>    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource<br>    has to be generated while uploading the PSU authentication data.<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithEncryptedPsuAuthentication':<br>    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource has<br>    to be generated while uploading the encrypted PSU authentication data.<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection':<br>    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource<br>    has to be generated while selecting the authentication method.<br>    This link is contained under exactly the same conditions as the data element 'scaMethods'<br>  * 'startAuthorisationWithTransactionAuthorisation':<br>    The link to the authorisation end-point, where the authorisation sub-resource<br>    has to be generated while authorising the transaction e.g. by uploading an<br>    OTP received by SMS.<br>  * 'self':<br>    The link to the payment initiation resource created by this request.<br>    This link can be used to retrieve the resource data.<br>  * 'status':<br>    The link to retrieve the transaction status of the payment initiation.<br>  * 'scaStatus':<br>    The link to retrieve the scaStatus of the corresponding authorisation sub-resource.<br>    This link is only contained, if an authorisation sub-resource has been already created.<br>|
|consents|[consentIdList](#schemaconsentidlist)|false|none|A list of consentIds.|
|payments|[paymentIdList](#schemapaymentidlist)|false|none|A list of paymentIds.|
|transactionStatus|[transactionStatus_SBS](#schematransactionstatus_sbs)|true|none|The transaction status is filled with codes of the ISO 20022 data table.<br>Only the codes RCVD, PATC, ACTC, ACWC and RJCT are used:<br>- 'ACSP': 'AcceptedSettlementInProcess' -<br>  All preceding checks such as technical validation and customer profile were successful and therefore the payment initiation has been accepted for execution.<br>- 'ACTC': 'AcceptedTechnicalValidation' -<br>  Authentication and syntactical and semantical validation are successful.<br>- 'ACWC': 'AcceptedWithChange' -<br>  Instruction is accepted but a change will be made, such as date or remittance not sent.<br>- 'RCVD': 'Received' -<br>  Payment initiation has been received by the receiving agent.<br>- 'RJCT': 'Rejected' -<br>  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation has been rejected.<br>|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|transactionStatus|ACSC|
|transactionStatus|ACTC|
|transactionStatus|PATC|
|transactionStatus|RCVD|
|transactionStatus|RJCT|
|transactionStatus|CANC|

|transactionStatus|[transactionStatus_SBS](#schematransactionstatus_sbs)|true|none|The transaction status is filled with codes of the ISO 20022 data table.<br>Only the codes RCVD, PATC, ACTC, ACWC and RJCT are used:<br>- 'ACSP': 'AcceptedSettlementInProcess' -<br>  All preceding checks such as technical validation and customer profile were successful and therefore the payment initiation has been accepted for execution.<br>- 'ACTC': 'AcceptedTechnicalValidation' -<br>  Authentication and syntactical and semantical validation are successful.<br>- 'ACWC': 'AcceptedWithChange' -<br>  Instruction is accepted but a change will be made, such as date or remittance not sent.<br>- 'RCVD': 'Received' -<br>  Payment initiation has been received by the receiving agent.<br>- 'RJCT': 'Rejected' -<br>  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation has been rejected.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|transactionStatus|ACSC|
|transactionStatus|ACTC|
|transactionStatus|PATC|
|transactionStatus|RCVD|
|transactionStatus|RJCT|
|transactionStatus|CANC|

<h2 id="tocS_standingOrderDetails">standingOrderDetails</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastandingorderdetails"></a>
<a id="schema_standingOrderDetails"></a>
<a id="tocSstandingorderdetails"></a>
<a id="tocsstandingorderdetails"></a>

```json
{
  "dayOfExecution": "1",
  "endDate": "1970-01-01",
  "executionRule": "following",
  "frequency": "Daily",
  "limitAmount": {
    "amount": "123",
    "currency": "EUR"
  },
  "monthsOfExecution": [
    "1"
  ],
  "multiplicator": 0,
  "startDate": "1970-01-01",
  "withinAMonthFlag": true
}
```

Details of underlying standing orders.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dayOfExecution|[dayOfExecution](#schemadayofexecution)|false|none|Day of execution as string.<br><br>This string consists of up two characters.<br>Leading zeroes are not allowed.<br><br>31 is ultimo of the month.<br>|
|endDate|[endDate](#schemaenddate)|false|none|The last applicable day of execution.<br>If not given, it is an infinite standing order.<br>|
|executionRule|[executionRule](#schemaexecutionrule)|false|none|"following" or "preceding" supported as values.<br>This data attribute defines the behaviour when recurring payment dates falls on a weekend or bank holiday.<br>The payment is then executed either the "preceding" or "following" working day.<br>ASPSP might reject the request due to the communicated value, if rules in Online-Banking are not supporting<br>this execution rule.<br>|
|frequency|[frequencyCode](#schemafrequencycode)|true|none|The following codes from the "EventFrequency7Code" of ISO 20022 are supported:<br>- "Daily"<br>- "Weekly"<br>- "EveryTwoWeeks"<br>- "Monthly"<br>- "EveryTwoMonths"<br>- "Quarterly"<br>- "SemiAnnual"<br>- "Annual"<br>- "MonthlyVariable"<br>|
|limitAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|none|
|monthsOfExecution|[monthsOfExecution](#schemamonthsofexecution)|false|none|The format is following the regular expression \d{1,2}. <br>The array is restricted to 11 entries. <br>The values contained in the array entries shall all be different and the maximum value of one entry is 12.<br>This attribute is contained if and only if the frequency equals "MonthlyVariable".<br>Example: An execution on January, April and October each year is addressed by ["1", "4", "10"].<br>|
|multiplicator|integer|false|none|This is multiplying the given frequency resulting the exact frequency,<br>e.g. Frequency=weekly and multiplicator=3 means every 3 weeks.<br>Remark: This attribute is rarely supported in the market.<br>|
|startDate|[startDate](#schemastartdate)|true|none|The first applicable day of execution starting from this date is the first payment.<br>|
|withinAMonthFlag|boolean|false|none|This element is only used in case of frequency equals "Monthly".<br><br>If this element equals false it has no effect.<br>If this element equals true, then the execution rule is overruled if the day of execution would fall into a different month using the execution rule.<br><br>Example: executionRule equals "preceding", dayOfExecution equals "02" and the second of a month is a Sunday. <br>In this case, the transaction date would be on the last day of the month before.<br> This would be overruled if withinAMonthFlag equals true and the payment is processed on Monday the third of the Month.<br>Remark: This attribute is rarely supported in the market.<br>|

```json
    },

      "href": "/v1/payments/swiss-sepa-credit-transfers/1234-wertiq-983"
    },
    "startAuthorisationWithEncryptedPsuAuthentication": {
      "href": "/v1/payments/swiss-sepa-credit-transfers/1234-wertiq-983"
    },
    "startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication": {
      "href": "/v1/payments/swiss-sepa-credit-transfers/1234-wertiq-983"
    },
    "updatePsuIdentification": {
      "href": "/v1/payments/swiss-sepa-credit-transfers/1234-wertiq-983"
    },
    "property1": {
      "href": "/v1/payments/swiss-sepa-credit-transfers/1234-wertiq-983"

  "challengeData": {

      "string"
    ],

  },

    "authenticationType": "SMS_OTP",
    "authenticationVersion": "string",
    "explanation": "Detailed information about the SCA method for the PSU.",

  },
  "psuMessage": "string",
  "scaMethods": [
    {
      "authenticationMethodId": "myAuthenticationID",
      "authenticationType": "SMS_OTP",
      "authenticationVersion": "string",
      "explanation": "Detailed information about the SCA method for the PSU.",
      "name": "SMS OTP on phone +49160 xxxxx 28"
    }
  ],
  "scaStatus": "psuAuthenticated"
}
```

Body of the JSON response for a Start SCA authorisation request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksStartScaProcess](#schema_linksstartscaprocess)|true|none|A list of hyperlinks to be recognised by the TPP. The actual hyperlinks used in the<br>response depend on the dynamical decisions of the ASPSP when processing the request.<br><br>**Remark:** All links can be relative or full links, to be decided by the ASPSP.<br><br>Type of links admitted in this response, (further links might be added for ASPSP defined<br>extensions):<br><br>- 'scaRedirect':<br>  In case of an SCA Redirect Approach, the ASPSP is transmitting the link to which to<br>  redirect the PSU browser.<br>- 'scaOAuth':<br>  In case of a SCA OAuth2 Approach, the ASPSP is transmitting the URI where the configuration of the Authorisation Server can be retrieved. The configuration follows the OAuth 2.0 Authorisation Server Metadata specification.<br>* 'confirmation': <br>  Might be added by the ASPSP if either the "scaRedirect" or "scaOAuth" hyperlink is returned <br>  in the same response message. <br>  This hyperlink defines the URL to the resource which needs to be updated with <br>    * a confirmation code as retrieved after the plain redirect authentication process with the ASPSP authentication server or<br>    * an access token as retrieved by submitting an authorization code after the integrated OAuth based authentication process with the ASPSP authentication server.<br>- 'updatePsuIdentification': <br>  The link to the authorisation or cancellation authorisation sub-resource, <br>  where PSU identification data needs to be uploaded.<br>- 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication':<br>  The link to the authorisation or cancellation authorisation sub-resource,<br>  where PSU authentication data needs to be uploaded.<br>- 'startAuthorisationWithEncryptedPsuAuthentication':<br>    Same as startAuthorisactionWithPsuAuthentication where the authentication data need to be encrypted on<br>    application layer in uploading.<br>- 'selectAuthenticationMethod':<br>  The link to the authorisation or cancellation authorisation sub-resource,<br>  where the selected authentication method needs to be uploaded.<br>  This link is contained under exactly the same conditions as the data element 'scaMethods'.<br>- 'authoriseTransaction':<br>  The link to the authorisation or cancellation authorisation sub-resource,<br>  where the authorisation data has to be uploaded, e.g. the TOP received by SMS.<br>- 'scaStatus':<br>  The link to retrieve the scaStatus of the corresponding authorisation sub-resource.<br>|
|authorisationId|[authorisationId](#schemaauthorisationid)|true|none|Resource identification of the related SCA.|
|challengeData|[challengeData](#schemachallengedata)|false|none|It is contained in addition to the data element 'chosenScaMethod' if challenge data is needed for SCA.<br>In rare cases this attribute is also used in the context of the 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication' link.<br>|
|chosenScaMethod|[authenticationObject](#schemaauthenticationobject)|false|none|Authentication object.<br>|
|psuMessage|[psuMessageText](#schemapsumessagetext)|false|none|Text to be displayed to the PSU.|
|scaMethods|[scaMethods](#schemascamethods)|false|none|This data element might be contained, if SCA is required and if the PSU has a choice between different<br>authentication methods.<br><br>Depending on the risk management of the ASPSP this choice might be offered before or after the PSU<br>has been identified with the first relevant factor, or if an access token is transported.<br><br>If this data element is contained, then there is also a hyperlink of type 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection'<br>contained in the response body.<br><br>These methods shall be presented towards the PSU for selection by the TPP.<br>|
|scaStatus|[scaStatus](#schemascastatus)|true|none|This data element is containing information about the status of the SCA method applied.<br><br>The following codes are defined for this data type.<br><br>  * 'received':<br>    An authorisation or cancellation-authorisation resource has been created successfully.<br>  * 'psuIdentified':<br>    The PSU related to the authorisation or cancellation-authorisation resource has been identified.<br>  * 'psuAuthenticated':<br>    The PSU related to the authorisation or cancellation-authorisation resource has been identified and authenticated e.g. by a password or by an access token.<br>  * 'scaMethodSelected':<br>    The PSU/TPP has selected the related SCA routine.<br>    If the SCA method is chosen implicitly since only one SCA method is available,<br>    then this is the first status to be reported instead of 'received'.<br>  * 'unconfirmed':<br>    SCA is technically successfully finalised by the PSU, but the authorisation resource needs a confirmation command by the TPP yet. <br>  * 'started':<br>    The addressed SCA routine has been started.<br>  * 'finalised':<br>    The SCA routine has been finalised successfully (including a potential confirmation command). <br>    This is a final status of the authorisation resource.<br>  * 'failed':<br>    The SCA routine failed.<br>    This is a final status of the authorisation resource.<br>  * 'exempted':<br>    SCA was exempted for the related transaction, the related authorisation is successful.<br>    This is a final status of the authorisation resource.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|scaStatus|received|
|scaStatus|psuIdentified|
|scaStatus|psuAuthenticated|
|scaStatus|scaMethodSelected|
|scaStatus|started|
|scaStatus|unconfirmed|
|scaStatus|finalised|
|scaStatus|failed|
|scaStatus|exempted|

<h2 id="tocS_transactionFeeIndicator">transactionFeeIndicator</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransactionfeeindicator"></a>
<a id="schema_transactionFeeIndicator"></a>
<a id="tocStransactionfeeindicator"></a>
<a id="tocstransactionfeeindicator"></a>

```json
true
```

If equals 'true', the transaction will involve specific transaction cost as shown by the ASPSP in
their public price list or as agreed between ASPSP and PSU.
If equals 'false', the transaction will not involve additional specific transaction costs to the PSU unless the fee amount is given specifically in the data elements transactionFees and/or currencyConversionFees.
If this data element is not used, there is no information about transaction fees unless the fee amount is given explicitly in the data element transactionFees and/or currencyConversionFees.

<h2 id="tocS_transactionStatus">transactionStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransactionstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_transactionStatus"></a>
<a id="tocStransactionstatus"></a>
<a id="tocstransactionstatus"></a>

```json
"ACCP"
```

The transaction status is filled with codes of the ISO 20022 data table:
- 'ACCC': 'AcceptedSettlementCompleted' -
  Settlement on the creditor's account has been completed.
- 'ACCP': 'AcceptedCustomerProfile' -
  Preceding check of technical validation was successful.
  Customer profile check was also successful.
- 'ACSC': 'AcceptedSettlementCompleted' -
  Settlement on the debtoro?=s account has been completed.

  **Usage:** this can be used by the first agent to report to the debtor that the transaction has been completed.

  **Warning:** this status is provided for transaction status reasons, not for financial information.
  It can only be used after bilateral agreement.
- 'ACSP': 'AcceptedSettlementInProcess' -
  All preceding checks such as technical validation and customer profile were successful and therefore the payment initiation has been accepted for execution.
- 'ACTC': 'AcceptedTechnicalValidation' -
  Authentication and syntactical and semantical validation are successful.
- 'ACWC': 'AcceptedWithChange' -
  Instruction is accepted but a change will be made, such as date or remittance not sent.
- 'ACWP': 'AcceptedWithoutPosting' -
  Payment instruction included in the credit transfer is accepted without being posted to the creditor customero?=s account.
- 'RCVD': 'Received' -
  Payment initiation has been received by the receiving agent.
- 'PDNG': 'Pending' -
  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation is pending.
  Further checks and status update will be performed.
- 'RJCT': 'Rejected' -
  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation has been rejected.
- 'CANC': 'Cancelled'
  Payment initiation has been cancelled before execution
  Remark: This codeis accepted as new code by ISO20022.
- 'ACFC': 'AcceptedFundsChecked' -
  Preceding check of technical validation and customer profile was successful and an automatic funds check was positive .
  Remark: This code is accepted as new code by ISO20022.
- 'PATC': 'PartiallyAcceptedTechnical'
  Correct The payment initiation needs multiple authentications, where some but not yet all have been performed. Syntactical and semantical validations are successful.
  Remark: This code is accepted as new code by ISO20022.
- 'PART': 'PartiallyAccepted' -
  A number of transactions have been accepted, whereas another number of transactions have not yet achieved 'accepted' status.
  Remark: This code may be used only in case of bulk payments. It is only used in a situation where all mandated authorisations have been applied, but some payments have been rejected.

<h2 id="tocS_transactionStatus_SBS">transactionStatus_SBS</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransactionstatus_sbs"></a>
<a id="schema_transactionStatus_SBS"></a>
<a id="tocStransactionstatus_sbs"></a>
<a id="tocstransactionstatus_sbs"></a>

```json
"RCVD"
```

The transaction status is filled with codes of the ISO 20022 data table.
Only the codes RCVD, PATC, ACTC, ACWC and RJCT are used:
- 'ACSP': 'AcceptedSettlementInProcess' -
  All preceding checks such as technical validation and customer profile were successful and therefore the payment initiation has been accepted for execution.
- 'ACTC': 'AcceptedTechnicalValidation' -
  Authentication and syntactical and semantical validation are successful.
- 'ACWC': 'AcceptedWithChange' -
  Instruction is accepted but a change will be made, such as date or remittance not sent.
- 'RCVD': 'Received' -
  Payment initiation has been received by the receiving agent.
- 'RJCT': 'Rejected' -
  Payment initiation or individual transaction included in the payment initiation has been rejected.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksTransactionDetails](#schema_linkstransactiondetails)|false|none|none|
|additionalInformation|[additionalInformation](#schemaadditionalinformation)|false|none|Might be used by the ASPSP to transport additional transaction related information to the PSU<br>|
|additionalInformationStructured|[additionalInformationStructured](#schemaadditionalinformationstructured)|false|none|Is used if and only if the bookingStatus entry equals "information". <br>Every active standing order related to the dedicated payment account result into one entry.<br>|
|balanceAfterTransaction|[balance](#schemabalance)|false|none|A single balance element.<br>|
|bankTransactionCode|[bankTransactionCode](#schemabanktransactioncode)|false|none|Bank transaction code as used by the ASPSP and using the sub elements of this structured code defined by ISO 20022.<br><br>This code type is concatenating the three ISO20022 Codes<br>  * Domain Code,<br>  * Family Code, and<br>  * SubFamiliy Code<br>by hyphens, resulting in 'DomainCode'-'FamilyCode'-'SubFamilyCode'.<br>|
|batchIndicator|boolean|false|none|If this indicator equals true, then the related entry is a batch entry.<br>|
|batchNumberOfTransactions|integer|false|none|Shall be used if and only if the batchIndicator is contained and equals true.<br>|
|bookingDate|[bookingDate](#schemabookingdate)|false|none|The date when an entry is posted to an account on the ASPSPs books.<br>|
|checkId|string|false|none|Identification of a Cheque.|
|creditorAccount|[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)|false|none|Reference to an account by either<br>  * IBAN, of a payment accounts, or<br>  * otherAccountIdentification, for payment accounts if there is no IBAN<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 CashAccount16-CH_IdTpCcy<br>|
|creditorAgent|[bicfi](#schemabicfi)|false|none|BICFI<br>|
|creditorId|[creditorId](#schemacreditorid)|false|none|Identification of Creditors, e.g. a SEPA Creditor ID.|
|creditorName|[creditorName](#schemacreditorname)|false|none|Creditor name.|
|currencyExchange|[reportExchangeRateList](#schemareportexchangeratelist)|false|none|Array of exchange rates.|
|debtorAccount|[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)|false|none|Reference to an account by either<br>  * IBAN, of a payment accounts, or<br>  * otherAccountIdentification, for payment accounts if there is no IBAN<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 CashAccount16-CH_IdTpCcy<br>|
|debtorAgent|[bicfi](#schemabicfi)|false|none|BICFI<br>|
|debtorName|[debtorName](#schemadebtorname)|false|none|Debtor name.|
|endToEndId|string|false|none|Unique end to end identity.|
|entryDetails|[entryDetails](#schemaentrydetails)|false|none|Might be used by the ASPSP to transport details about transactions within a batch.<br>|
|entryReference|[entryReference](#schemaentryreference)|false|none|Is the identification of the transaction as used e.g. for reference for deltafunction on application level.<br>The same identification as for example used within camt.05x messages.<br>|
|mandateId|string|false|none|Identification of Mandates, e.g. a SEPA Mandate ID.|
|proprietaryBankTransactionCode|[proprietaryBankTransactionCode](#schemaproprietarybanktransactioncode)|false|none|Proprietary bank transaction code as used within a community or within an ASPSP e.g.<br>for MT94x based transaction reports.<br>|
|purposeCode|[purposeCode](#schemapurposecode)|false|none|ExternalPurpose1Code from ISO 20022.<br><br>Values from ISO 20022 External Code List ExternalCodeSets_1Q2018 June 2018.<br>|
|remittanceInformationStructured|[remittanceInformationStructuredMax140](#schemaremittanceinformationstructuredmax140)|false|none|Structured remittance information Max<br>|
|remittanceInformationStructuredArray|[remittanceInformationStructuredArray](#schemaremittanceinformationstructuredarray)|false|none|Array of structured remittance information.<br>|
|remittanceInformationUnstructured|[remittanceInformationUnstructured](#schemaremittanceinformationunstructured)|false|none|Unstructured remittance information.<br>|
|remittanceInformationUnstructuredArray|[remittanceInformationUnstructuredArray](#schemaremittanceinformationunstructuredarray)|false|none|Array of unstructured remittance information.<br>|
|transactionAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|none|
|transactionId|[transactionId](#schematransactionid)|false|none|This identification is given by the attribute transactionId of the corresponding entry of a transaction list.<br>|
|ultimateCreditor|[ultimateCreditor](#schemaultimatecreditor)|false|none|Ultimate creditor.|
|ultimateDebtor|[ultimateDebtor](#schemaultimatedebtor)|false|none|Ultimate debtor.|
|valueDate|string(date)|false|none|The Date at which assets become available to the account owner in case of a credit.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|purposeCode|SALA|
|purposeCode|PENS|


Body of the JSON response for a successful read transaction list request.
This account report contains transactions resulting from the query parameters.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|[_linksDownload](#schema_linksdownload)|false|none|A list of hyperlinks to be recognised by the TPP.<br><br>Type of links admitted in this response:<br>  - "download": a link to a resource, where the transaction report might be downloaded from in<br>  case where transaction reports have a huge size.<br><br>Remark: This feature shall only be used where camt-data is requested which has a huge size.<br>|
|account|[accountReference16-CH](#schemaaccountreference16-ch)|false|none|Reference to an account by either<br>  * IBAN, of a payment accounts, or<br>  * otherAccountIdentification, for payment accounts if there is no IBAN<br>adapted from ISO pain.001.001.03.ch.02 CashAccount16-CH_IdTpCcy<br>|
|balances|[balanceList](#schemabalancelist)|false|none|A list of balances regarding this account, e.g. the current balance, the last booked balance.<br>The list might be restricted to the current balance.<br>|
|transactions|[accountReport](#schemaaccountreport)|false|none|JSON based account report.<br>This account report contains transactions resulting from the query parameters.<br><br>'booked' shall be contained if bookingStatus parameter is set to "booked" or "both".<br><br>'pending' is not contained if the bookingStatus parameter is set to "booked" or "information".<br><br>'information' Only contained if the bookingStatus is set to "information" and if supported by ASPSP.<br>|

<a id="tocstrustedbeneficiaryflag"></a>

```json
false
```

Additional Service: Trusted Benificiaries
Within this data element, the ASPSP might optionally communicate towards the TPP whether the creditor was part of the related trusted beneficiary list. 
This attribute is only contained in case of a final scaStatus.

|_links|[_linksUpdatePsuAuthentication](#schema_linksupdatepsuauthentication)|false|none|A list of hyperlinks to be recognised by the TPP. Might be contained, if several authentication methods<br>are available for the PSU.<br>Type of links admitted in this response:<br>  * 'updateAdditionalPsuAuthentication':<br>    The link to the payment initiation or account information resource,<br>    which needs to be updated by an additional PSU password.<br>    This link is only contained in rare cases,<br>    where such additional passwords are needed for PSU authentications.<br>  * 'updateAdditionalEncryptedPsuAuthentication':<br>    The link to the payment initiation or account information resource,<br>    which needs to be updated by an additional encrypted PSU password.<br>    This link is only contained in rare cases, where such additional passwords are needed for PSU authentications.<br>  * 'selectAuthenticationMethod':<br>    This is a link to a resource, where the TPP can select the applicable second factor authentication<br>    methods for the PSU, if there were several available authentication methods.<br>    This link is only contained, if the PSU is already identified or authenticated with the first relevant<br>    factor or alternatively an access token, if SCA is required and if the PSU has a choice between different<br>    authentication methods.<br>    If this link is contained, then there is also the data element 'scaMethods' contained in the response body.<br>  * 'authoriseTransaction': <br>    The link to the resource, where the "Transaction authorisation request" is sent to. <br>    This is the link to the resource which will authorise the transaction by checking the SCA authentication <br>    data within the Embedded SCA approach.<br>  * 'scaStatus':<br>    The link to retrieve the scaStatus of the corresponding authorisation sub-resource.<br>|
|authorisationId|[authorisationId](#schemaauthorisationid)|false|none|Resource identification of the related SCA.|
|challengeData|[challengeData](#schemachallengedata)|false|none|It is contained in addition to the data element 'chosenScaMethod' if challenge data is needed for SCA.<br>In rare cases this attribute is also used in the context of the 'startAuthorisationWithPsuAuthentication' link.<br>|
|chosenScaMethod|[authenticationObject](#schemaauthenticationobject)|false|none|Authentication object.<br>|
|currencyConversionFees|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|none|
|estimatedInterbankSettlementAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|none|
|estimatedTotalAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|none|
|psuMessage|[psuMessageText](#schemapsumessagetext)|false|none|Text to be displayed to the PSU.|
|scaMethods|[scaMethods](#schemascamethods)|false|none|This data element might be contained, if SCA is required and if the PSU has a choice between different<br>authentication methods.<br><br>Depending on the risk management of the ASPSP this choice might be offered before or after the PSU<br>has been identified with the first relevant factor, or if an access token is transported.<br><br>If this data element is contained, then there is also a hyperlink of type 'startAuthorisationWithAuthenticationMethodSelection'<br>contained in the response body.<br><br>These methods shall be presented towards the PSU for selection by the TPP.<br>|
|scaStatus|[scaStatus](#schemascastatus)|true|none|This data element is containing information about the status of the SCA method applied.<br><br>The following codes are defined for this data type.<br><br>  * 'received':<br>    An authorisation or cancellation-authorisation resource has been created successfully.<br>  * 'psuIdentified':<br>    The PSU related to the authorisation or cancellation-authorisation resource has been identified.<br>  * 'psuAuthenticated':<br>    The PSU related to the authorisation or cancellation-authorisation resource has been identified and authenticated e.g. by a password or by an access token.<br>  * 'scaMethodSelected':<br>    The PSU/TPP has selected the related SCA routine.<br>    If the SCA method is chosen implicitly since only one SCA method is available,<br>    then this is the first status to be reported instead of 'received'.<br>  * 'unconfirmed':<br>    SCA is technically successfully finalised by the PSU, but the authorisation resource needs a confirmation command by the TPP yet. <br>  * 'started':<br>    The addressed SCA routine has been started.<br>  * 'finalised':<br>    The SCA routine has been finalised successfully (including a potential confirmation command). <br>    This is a final status of the authorisation resource.<br>  * 'failed':<br>    The SCA routine failed.<br>    This is a final status of the authorisation resource.<br>  * 'exempted':<br>    SCA was exempted for the related transaction, the related authorisation is successful.<br>    This is a final status of the authorisation resource.<br>|
|transactionFees|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_validUntil">validUntil</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavaliduntil"></a>
<a id="schema_validUntil"></a>
<a id="tocSvaliduntil"></a>
<a id="tocsvaliduntil"></a>

```json
"2020-12-31"
```

This parameter is defining a valid until date (including the mentioned date) for the requested consent. 
The content is the local ASPSP date in ISO-Date format, e.g. 2017-10-30.

Future dates might get adjusted by ASPSP. 

If a maximal available date is requested, a date in far future is to be used: "9999-12-31". 

In both cases the consent object to be retrieved by the get consent request will contain the adjusted date.
